stories.title: Reed Sheppard gets paid… well, kind of
stories.summary: Big news for Reed
stories.detailText: Yesterday afternoon, Adam Spolane reported that the Houston Rockets had picked up Reed Sheppard’s fourth-year option. This means for the 2027-2028 season, Sheppard will be making just above $14 million before he is eligible for a rookie contract extension. It could be seen as an odd move for the Rockets, who had some questions about where Sheppard would fit into the rotation throughout this season, but it does seem like they want to keep him around for at least this year and next year before potentially extending him in free agency after the 2027 season. Sheppard is the 10th first-round pick the Rockets have selected from 2021-24. He is the sixth of 10 players to have his fourth-year option picked up by the team. The previous five, Jalen Green, Alperen Sengun, Jabari Smith Jr., Tari Eason and Amen Thompson, all inked contract extensions with Houston. After a rough debut year, Sheppard has become a fixture in the Rockets’ rotation. He moved into being Fred VanVleet’s backup at point guard from sliding completely out of the rotation. He also played three games for the Rockets’ G League team in Rio Grande Valley in January 2025 to get more playing time. The Rockets feel Sheppard still can play point guard at an NBA level, but with VanVleet returning and Marcus Smart joining the team as a free agent, he’s been playing largely off the ball through four games this season. “He’s a guy that has to get better at pick and roll,” Rockets head coach Ime Udoka stated on media day. “He’s played off-ball his whole life, and you know he’s really good at it. Numbers-wise, Sheppard does seem to have the ability to contribute as a scorer, playmaker and at times on the perimeter defensively, but he does need to figure out a way to be able to be a lot more efficient with his shooting from the field and from three. Sheppard is definitely capable of improving his efficiency this year if he can play more off-ball and take advantage of playmakers like Fred VanVleet and Alperen Sengun, who can both set up Sheppard with great catch-and-shoot situations to create more separation from the defense when coming off screens and cuts. Sheppard might also develop as a shooter, just by acquiring more confidence over the season. It should also be noted that Sheppard has had some injuries this season, including a left knee issue that helped him out against the San Antonio Spurs on October 23, and a back injury that kept him out of the lineup against the Dallas Mavericks. The injuries Sheppard has suffered so far this year don’t appear to be severe, but they are crucial to keep in mind in case it is impacting his play on the court when he is available. It is clear that the front office has belief in Reed Sheppard, and time will tell to see how he develops this season and beyond.

stories.title: Lakers' Jeanie Buss accuses siblings of 'cloak and dagger' tactics
stories.summary: Jeanie Buss accused her siblings of conspiring against her in court filings responding to her siblings' ongoing effort to sell their shares in the Lakers.
stories.detailText: In a court filing this week, Jeanie Buss accused her siblings of conspiring against her in a "cloak and dagger" campaign through the media, said they were jealous that their father picked her over them to govern the Los Angeles Lakers and asked a judge to block her siblings' attempt to sell the family's shares in the team, which would end her run as the Lakers' governor. Wednesday's filing, reviewed by ESPN, is the latest salvo in the bitter legal battle playing out between Jeanie and her siblings, namely Joey and Jesse Buss, leading up to a scheduled Dec. 8 hearing in Los Angeles Superior Court. The filing responds to recent filings by Jeanie's siblings, who are seeking to sell the family's remaining shares of the Lakers to the Bob Iger and Josh Kushner ownership group, which is seeking to buy the team from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. "The conflicts that ensued after Dr. [Jerry] Buss's death [in 2013] were sadly inevitable, and no doubt intensified given that Dr. Buss chose his daughter over four sons to be his successor," Jeanie's lawyers wrote in the Wednesday filing. "Respondents' obsession with tearing down Jeanie and their inability to accept that she would be a part of the Lakers' future is borne of this classic succession parable." In 2025, Walter bought a majority stake in the Lakers from the Buss family at a $10 billion valuation. During that sale, the Buss family retained a 17.82% stake, just above the NBA's 15% minimum for the family to retain control. The family also received go-along rights. On Aug. 17, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Johnny, Jim, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss had voted to sell the remaining family shares to Iger and Kushner using those go-along rights. Each sibling stands to make an additional $371 million if the family sells the entirety of its shares via the go-along provision. Jeanie has attempted to block those attempts to sell, saying that her siblings must obey a 2017 court order that required the two co-trustees, Janie and Joey, to always vote to ensure she remained the controlling owner of the team. In Wednesday's filing, she again asked the court to remove Joey and Janie as co-trustees of the trust for breach of fiduciary duty, to hold them in contempt of court, to find Jim, Johnny and Jesse liable for aiding and abetting a violation of the 2017 court order, and for her to be reimbursed for legal costs. Sources close to the family have told ESPN that there have been settlement talks between the two sides, but it's unclear how much progress has been made leading up to the scheduled December hearing. "Jeanie had no choice but to seek court intervention to enforce the clear terms of the trust and this court's 2017 order," Wednesday's filing states. "Respondents respond [by] casting themselves as victims, when in reality, the entire episode is their own false flag operation. "The cloak and dagger, backroom 'votes' and 'resolutions' shared with ESPN, rather than their co-trustee and sister, and subsequent refusal to discuss the matter, was intended to force Jeanie's hand, cry victim and again smear her in the media by sharing in advance their specious response." In previous filings, the siblings have said that Jeanie's stance lacks merit and have asked the court to dismiss the claim while arguing that they exercised voting rights expressly granted to them as beneficiaries. "There is deep irony in [Jeanie] alleging that it is [Joey and Janie] who are putting their self-interests first," an Oct. 16 filing by the siblings stated, as reported by ESPN's Dave McMenamin. "The entire petition [originally filed by Jeanie] is predicated on the notion that rights expressly granted to the beneficiaries by [the trust] should be subjugated to [Jeanie's] personal interest in remaining controlling owner. [Jeanie's] hypocrisy should not go unnoticed." In Wednesday's filing, Jeanie responded, "It drips with irony that Respondents' thesis is that Jeanie is self-interested. Jeanie's 'self-interest' has been to lead as her father and mother directed in their trusts." On Friday, ESPN's Ramona Shelburne reported that, technically, go-along rights can be invoked only after Walter officially notifies the family that he has signed a deal to sell. That same day, Shelburne also reported -- citing sources close to the negotiation -- that Walter and Kushner have agreed on all outstanding terms of the sale of the team and are expected to sign the formal agreement soon. Once it is signed, it will be reviewed by the NBA.

stories.title: LeBron James, Joel Embiid both out for 76ers vs. Hornets
stories.summary: LeBron James and Joel Embiid are out for the Sixers on Saturday in the second game of a back-to-back. It's the first time Philly is without both players at the same time.
stories.detailText: Philadelphia 76ers stars LeBron James and Joel Embiid will miss Saturday's road game against the Charlotte Hornets with injury management, the team announced. James's injury designation is low back/sciatica and Embiid's is right foot plantar fasciitis. Charlotte is Philadelphia's second back-to-back of the season; it's expected that the Sixers will continue to be cautious with playing Embiid and James on back-to-backs as they navigate a long season. Still, this will be the first game that these two miss together. Each has missed one game with injury management, but not simultaneously so far this season. Jaylen Brown , who missed Friday night's home win over the New York Knicks with a left patella injury, is listed as questionable. Center Tacko Fall (quad) and forward/center Jabari Walker (knee) were listed as questionable. Fall hasn't played a game yet this season, and Walker hasn't played since injuring his knee in the team's win against the Milwaukee Bucks last Saturday. Coach Nick Nurse said James had his "best game" of the season in Friday night's win over the Knicks. It was his first 20-point game as a Sixer, as he finished with 20 points, nine rebounds and eight assists.

stories.title: Collin Gillespie is showing Jalen Green how to run the Suns
stories.summary: Four games into the season, Gillespie is making a compelling case to handle the ball when the Suns need it most.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX, AZ - OCTOBER 30: Collin Gillespie #12 of the Phoenix Suns handles the ball during the game against the Denver Nuggets during the 2026 Emirates NBA Cup on October 30, 2026 at Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Kate Frese/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The season is young for the Phoenix Suns, and every game offers another chance to learn more about this team and whether it can execute its vision in a way that translates to winning. Thus far, it’s been rough. Phoenix is off to a 1-3 start, and if you take a look at the defensive rating, it certainly feels like Halloween. Because those numbers are downright spooky. Last in defensive rating at 125.8, last in opposing three-point percentage at 43.9%, last in opposing second-chance points at 22.3. You don’t want to make rash decisions based on individual performances during the infancy of a season, but at some point you need to recognize that whatever this version of the Suns is isn’t working. At least not yet. Should patience be exercised? Perhaps, and we begrudgingly know it will. Until an internal threshold relative to either games or minutes has been crossed, this experiment in futility marches forward, with each night serving as a quiz to examine. What did Friday’s night pop quiz teach us? It reinforces something we’ve known since we first started watching, playing, and consuming this glorious sport: teams function better when roles are clearly defined. “Positionless” basketball is a lazy term for those who support teams that do not possess defined roles. For teams with duplicative archetypes in the same starting lineup. “It’s gonna make sense,” one will say of the starting five. “Why?” a curious and befuddled onlooker will question. “Because the NBA is now ‘positionless’”. I’m guilty. I’ve bought into the cheap trick and five-dollar fantasy that positionless basketball could equate to success. I purchased some stock in the belief that a Booker/Beal backcourt could be productive, and it’s why I’ve been cautious about the Booker/Green backcourt since its inception. Fool me once, shame on me n’ such. Sure, you can have a pair of combo guards in the backcourt, but they still need to have defined roles, defined areas of space in which they operate, and one better be pretty damn good at being the primary ball handler. Some call those roles “positions”. Positionless basketball is something that has become a product of the AAU circuit, where young players are encouraged to pad their statistics because, ultimately, those numbers help them get noticed and create opportunities to make it big one day. With the NIL era upon us, getting noticed has become even more financially important. Somewhere along the way, traditional point guard play, facilitation, and distribution have become less of a priority. Those are the things that make everyone around you better, even if they don’t always show up in the box score. Within the concept of positionless basketball, there still needs to be an understanding of roles and, more importantly, who is actually capable of executing them. What we witnessed Friday night, and quite frankly what we’ve seen throughout a season and a half, is another reminder that this offense simply functions better when Collin Gillespie is involved. He’s not a traditional point guard, but he excels in that role. That’s what the Suns need right now. Why? Because Jalen Green was having an off night, something that has unfortunately plagued him throughout his career. Consistently, he’s been inconsistent. 20 points on 8-of-13 shooting against OKC, 2 points on 1-of-6 shooting against Denver. When you look at his career scoring trend, you see dots scattered about like duck shot on an outhouse. I can’t blame the young lad. This team wants Jalen Green to be a facilitator, to essentially play point guard. And when you’re forced into an unfamiliar role, it takes time to adjust. Unfortunately, point guard is one of the most difficult positions to play in the NBA. It requires selflessness, court awareness, and the ability to process information at an incredibly high speed. You can almost feel Jalen thinking out there early this season. He’s trying to read the defense, make the right decision, and execute what’s being asked of him. And the best flashes we’ve seen? They come when he stops thinking and starts reacting. That’s his superpower. His instincts, explosiveness, and ability to attack without hesitation are what make him dangerous. It reminds me of Ryan Dunn, who’s being asked to become a true 3-and-D player despite that not necessarily being what his natural skill set lends itself to. Once again, the Suns find themselves asking a player to become something he isn’t , rather than maximizing what he already does well. And in the process, they’re diminishing the very qualities that make him valuable. Green is better off the ball, operating as a piece of the offense rather than being the driving force behind it. Therein lies the roster construction conundrum we’ve been staring at for two seasons: 57% of your cap is tied up in duplicative players. Because the same could be said about Devin Booker. He excels when his role is not the offensive facilitating fulcrum. That, my fellow Suns’ citizens, is criticism I’ll save for another day… We heard throughout the offseason that Green had spent time working with Steve Nash , with the goal of improving his ability to read opposing defenses and make quicker decisions. Early this season, it’s apparent that his processing is taking a split second too long. His assist percentage is 14.1% (33rd percentile), his assist-to-turnover ratio is 1.3 (14th percentile), and his assist points created is 6.0 per game (25th percentile). In the NBA, where you’re facing elite athleticism and basketball IQ night after night, a split second can make all the difference in the trajectory of a career. Unfortunately, when you’re looking for someone to make high basketball IQ plays with split-second decision-making, Green typically isn’t the first player who comes to mind. It’s a reminder that Jalen Green entered the NBA following his time with the developmental G League Ignite as a player whose greatest asset was his elite athleticism. He jumped off the high school screen with his explosiveness, his ability to finish around the basket, his shooting potential, and his impressive physical tools. He possessed the kind of raw talent that makes scouts salivate and front offices dream about what a player could eventually become. His career thus far has been relatively average, with much of his scoring production coming through volume rather than efficiency. The physical gifts are undeniable. The challenge has been turning those gifts into consistently productive basketball. Collin Gillespie took an entirely different path. He went from fighting for an opportunity on a two-way contract to earning a fully guaranteed deal and eventually a contract extension. And what keeps him on the floor? It certainly isn’t elite athleticism. It’s his defensive effort, his ability to read the floor offensively, his understanding of how to operate within a system, and his efficiency, particularly from beyond the arc. So why am I bringing up the career paths of these two players? Because they represent two fundamentally different approaches to succeeding in the NBA. Green entered the league relying on extraordinary athleticism and the freedom to operate outside traditional positional responsibilities. Gillespie has built his career by understanding those responsibilities, embracing them, and executing within the structure around him. One was given opportunities because of what his physical gifts suggested he could become. The other earned his opportunities by consistently demonstrating that he understood exactly what his team needed him to be. Collin Gillespie is more comfortable handling the ball, navigating his way through defenses, creating mismatches, and reading what the opposition is doing as those opportunities develop. Through four games this season, his assist percentage is 18.1% (38th percentile), his assist-to-turnover ratio is 3.3 (36th percentile), and his assist points created is 14.5 per game (64th percentile). Not gaudy numbers, but certainly improvements over what Green has provided in this small sample size to start the 2026-27 season. Friday night was a reminder of this. Against Denver, during his first six minutes on the floor, Green and the Suns were a -3. Gillespie entered, and over the next nine minutes, Phoenix was a +7. That trend continued throughout the game . The team was chunky when Green was on the floor, fluid when Gillespie was present. When Green entered, the offense tended to sputter. This isn’t solely his fault. The entire starting five was having trouble producing, as apparent from the rotations showcased above. When he and Devin Booker shared the court, roles were not defined, and the team had a -19.8 net rating. When Booker was off the court and Green was tasked with the “bring the ball up the court” duties, the ball became sticky. The offense was less fluid. He’d dribble for a while, attack the basket, get blocked, and that was the possession. No movement, no opportunity for anyone else to get involved. Green killed the Suns’ momentum on that possession. Dribbled into a crowded paint, never looked to kick it out, and forced a shot that got blocked. Murray answered with a three. Green has to recognize when the defense collapses and move the ball. That’s a 5-point momentum swing. — John Voita, III (@DarthVoita) October 31, 2026 Through four games, albeit with a small sample size, Green possesses a minus-28.3 net rating compared to Gillespie’s minus-2.3. And when you examine the on/off numbers, they speak for themselves. The defensive side of the ball will always be the weaker part of this argument because Green has the opportunity to provide more defensively due to his size. For all the heart Gillespie has, he’ll never possess the physical tools to be an elite defender, yet he’s still third in the league with 3.0 steals per game. When you look up and down the roster at the statistical output, particularly defensive rating, nobody on this team looks good. That’s what happens when you have the worst defense in the league. But there’s a significant difference between Jalen Green’s 133.3 defensive rating and Gillespie’s 120.7. So even on that end of the floor, Gillespie has been the better option. I’ve hit you with a ton of advanced metrics and lineup data, but do we really need all of that? We know what our eyes are telling us, and at the end of the day, they’re telling us that there’s considerably more fluidity offensively and more intensity defensively when Gillespie is on the floor instead of Green. This isn’t to suggest that the two players can’t coexist on the roster, because at this point in the season, they’re going to have to. The Suns will continue evaluating Green to determine whether he fits into what this team currently is and what it could eventually become. When you’re carrying a $36.3 million price tag, naturally, there’s going to be increased scrutiny surrounding your performance. We need to see a larger sample size, right? But in reality, do we? Because we’re beginning to witness some of the same trends we saw last season with Green… Remember the beginning of last year, when the Suns seemed to have a clear understanding of who they were? Green was injured for much of that stretch. When he returned, the team experienced some destabilization as it attempted to integrate him into the rotations and figure out how he fit. What’s going to happen in the upcoming games? We might not know, but we saw a hint Friday night of what Jordan Ott is beginning to experiment with. Collin Gillespie closed the game while Jalen Green watched from the bench because Ott recognized that, within the confines of that particular matchup, it gave the Suns their best opportunity to win. How long until there’s a realization that, from an organizational standpoint, this might be the Suns’ best opportunity to win moving forward? Not surprisingly, the team is standing with Green. “We’ve got a ton of confidence in JG,” Collin Gillespie said of his teammate following the loss to Denver. “We’re riding with JG 100 times out of 100.” "We've got a ton of confidence in JG." Collin Gillespie's full comments on Jalen Green, who scored just two points on 1-of-6 shooting in 24 minutes of Suns loss to Nuggets. #Suns https://t.co/SeTCKuH6J3 pic.twitter.com/KoSbsUcfDc — Duane Rankin (@DuaneRankin) October 31, 2026 Moving Green to the bench is something I believe could benefit him. He’d be operating in a role much more conducive to his skill set, allowing him to focus on what he does best. But there’s also the potential for his ego to take a hit, and that’s the human element of this entire situation. It’s something we as fans have very little connectivity to when it comes to understanding the inner workings of the Phoenix Suns. There’s more to this than plugging and playing names into a roster. There are personalities involved, relationships to manage, and aspects of humility that need to be considered as well. Again, we’ve now experienced this for 36 games if you go back to last season, and the results continue to be disjointed and disconnected on both ends of the floor. Green isn’t the sole reason for that, either. When Devin Booker scores three points in one game and then follows it up with another performance in which he doesn’t appear particularly aggressive, finishing with only 20 points, there are clearly greater issues at play. There’s one common concern running through all of it: your highest-paid players aren’t providing the effort and production you need from them consistently. Maybe it’s too early to draw conclusions. My guess is that the franchise will give this another eight to ten games before seriously considering any drastic changes. Putting the human element aside for a moment, you eventually have to recognize who a player is, what he brings to the table, and whether his production matches the price you’re paying for it. We’re only four games into the season, but Jalen Green is shooting 28.6% from beyond the arc, possesses an assist percentage of only 14.1%, and has a defensive rating that’s in the shitter. Those aren’t encouraging numbers for someone who’s supposed to be your starting “point guard”, especially when the offense continues to struggle with connectivity and the defense remains a significant concern. For context, Devin Booker isn’t exactly lighting things up defensively himself, carrying a defensive rating of 137.2. At some point, the Suns have to decide whether they’re more committed to the idea of what Jalen Green could become or the reality of what Collin Gillespie already provides. Green can still be valuable, and finding a role that maximizes his strengths should remain a priority (although, at that price tag…yikes). But Phoenix needs someone who can organize the offense, make quick decisions, execute on the defensive end, and bring consistency to a lineup desperately searching for it. Gillespie has demonstrated that he can do those things. The question is how much longer Jordan Ott is willing to experiment before acknowledging what’s already working. Start. Collin. Gillespie. …and end games with him too — John Voita, III (@DarthVoita) October 31, 2026

stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 22: Jaylen Brown #7, LeBron James, and Joel Embiid #21 of the Philadelphia 76ers look on during the game against the Cleveland Cavaliers on October 22, 2026 at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images It’s likely time for the first game driven by VJ Maxx of the season. The Sixers released their injury report ahead of their Halloween showdown in Charlotte and have unsurprisingly ruled out Joel Embiid and LeBron James. Jaylen Brown, Jabari Walker and Tacko Fall are all listed as questionable. Brown missed Friday’s game against the New York Knicks with patellar tendinopathy in his left knee. Nick Nurse did not have any more information other than he wasn’t available. James and Embiid will get the second leg of the back-to-back off as expected. James is again listed with lower back/sciatica management, and Embiid again with plantar fasciitis management. The end of the bench remains banged up as well. Walker could miss his fourth straight game, also with patellar tendinopathy or jumper’s knee, as it’s typically referred to. Dominick Barlow remains out with his spine injury, but we could get out first look at Fall who’s been nursing a quad injury. For the Hornets, who are also playing the second half of a back-to-back, they’ve yet to see Kon Knueppel, Colby White or Grant Williams play this season thanks to preseason injuries. Knueppel appears close to a return, having been assigned to Charlotte’s G-League team to practice. The Hornets will be without them for this one, but will essentially trot out the same team that lost to the Washington Wizards Friday night in D.C. It should an interesting game. If the trio of James, Embiid and Brown are unable to play, we should see a whole lot of Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Dean Wade and Anfernee Simons. That trio has been excellent coming off the bench so far this season. What Nick Nurse does at center is anyone’s guess and will largely be dictated by the availability of Walker and Fall.

stories.title: Sources: Thunder no longer signing Ochai Agbaji following Chet Holmgren injury
stories.summary: The Thunder are no longer signing free agent Ochai Agbaji as the franchise takes a step back to reevaluate its open roster spot after losing Chet Holmgren for two-plus months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
stories.detailText: The Oklahoma City Thunder are no longer signing free agent Ochai Agbaji as the franchise takes a step back to reevaluate its open roster spot after losing Chet Holmgren for two-plus months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Oklahoma City had agreed Friday to sign Agbaji to fill its open roster spot after major injuries to guard Cason Wallace and forward Jalen Williams , but then the Thunder decided to reconsider the options following the determination that Holmgren would also be out for an extended period. Agbaji's health was not a concern or factor in the decision, sources said. Agbaji, the No. 14 pick in the 2022 draft, has averaged 7.2 points and 2.7 rebounds in 263 games, including 108 starts. Agbaji, 26, was waived by the New York Knicks in final roster cuts this month. He has played for three NBA teams in his four years, splitting last season with the Toronto Raptors and Brooklyn Nets . Williams (fractured fibula, dislocated left ankle) and Wallace (torn labrum in left shoulder) both suffered injuries during Sunday's win over the LA Clippers that required surgery. Their recoveries will both take several months, but the Thunder have not ruled either player out for the season. OKC expects Holmgren to return in eight to 10 weeks after undergoing biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear.

stories.title: VJ Edgecombe was ready for the moment yet again
stories.summary: VJ Edgecombe came up with a big stop then nailed a dagger three. It was just another day at the office for the 21-year-old.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 30: Vj Edgecombe #77 of the Philadelphia 76ers celebrates a three-pointer during the second half of an Emirates NBA Cup game against the New York Knicks at Xfinity Mobile Arena on October 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the main schools of thought stemming from the “there’s only one ball to go around” critique of this year’s Sixers team was that it would hinder the development of VJ Edgecombe, especially going into a crucial second season. Five games into his sophomore season and that hasn’t been a problem at all for the guard from Baylor. The Sixers have won all five games he’s appeared in and he’s made big plays down the stretch in just about all of them. As the New York Knicks looked prime to pull off a devastating comeback in Philadelphia, Edgecombe hit a three to extend the Sixers’ one-point lead to four with 32 seconds remaining. It’s the type of clutch shotmaking the coaching staff has come to expect from Edgecombe after he made a habit of it his rookie year. “He just does that, it’s really who he is,” head coach Nick Nurse said after the game. “We all know it.” Nurse, nor any Sixer, had a problem with Edgecombe taking that shot despite missing his previous three attempts from deep on the night. He plays with a level of fearlessness and confidence that’s earned that trust from his teammates. Even some of his newest teammates have picked on Edgecombe’s knack for big moments. “He doesn’t shy away from the moment,“ LeBron James said. ”[He’s a] young, young kid, but thrives in the moment.“ It was a bit relieving that it was a three ball from Edgecombe that saved the day. For all his contributions this season, shooting the ball from deep has been one of his rare struggles. He’s shot just 29% from three through his first five games of the campaign. “Early I haven’t been making a lot of threes, but they’re gonna fall, and I’m gonna keep shooting the ball,” Edgecombe said. “Tonight, even though I was 0-for-3 at the time, I still shot it. That’s just the confidence I have in myself.” What Edgecombe has done a great job of this year is using the attention of his superstar teammates to cut into wide open lanes and scoop up easy baskets. He’s also become one of the best rebounders on the team while usually guarding the other team’s best player. He’s done an especially good job cutting for Joel Embiid, a big reason Embiid is up to averaging 4.8 assists per game so far this season. “When they go double him, obviously you know teams gonna rotate,” Edgecombe said, “and so I just try to find that gap where I can cut or just find a window for him.” It’s the type of complementary basketball required to make a group with this much talent work together. Many worried before the season there wasn’t anywhere on the roster the Sixers would get those types of contributions from. “It’s great to just have those guys, those complementary guys out there on the floor where we can all complement one another,” James said. “‘Rese getting double teamed, VJ has the confidence that Tyrese gonna give him the ball and he can knock down shots and vice versa.” Edgecombe is clearly fifth in the pecking order in the healthy starting five when it comes to shot distribution, but that hasn’t stopped him from being one of their most important players when he’s on the floor. Being vital to helping a team with championship expectations pick up wins on a nightly basis has been just fine for his development so far.

stories.title: Thunder's Chet Holmgren out 8-10 weeks; OKC flips on Agbaji signing, per sources
stories.summary: Chet Holmgren will be out eight to 10 weeks because of a knee injury, the latest setback for a Thunder team that lost Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace for an extended time early this week.
stories.detailText: Star Oklahoma City Thunder power forward/center Chet Holmgren will miss eight to 10 weeks due to a patellar tendon tear in his right knee, the team said Friday night. Holmgren is the third Thunder starter to be ruled out for an extended period this week, joining forward Jalen Williams (fractured fibula, dislocated ankle) and guard Cason Wallace (torn labrum). According to the Thunder, Holmgren met with specialists after experiencing mild discomfort in his right knee Sunday -- the same day Williams and Wallace were hurt in a game against the LA Clippers . A determination was made to perform a "biological treatment" Friday to address what the team called a "small" tear. Holmgren's injury led the Thunder to no longer sign free agent forward Ochai Agbaji, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Saturday. Agbaji was set to join the Thunder following the injuries to Williams and Wallace, but the team is taking a step back to reevaluate its open roster spot, sources said. Agbaji's health was not a concern or factor in the decision, sources said. Holmgren has suffered three significant injuries since the Thunder selected the 7-footer with the No. 2 pick in the 2022 draft. He missed the 2022-23 season after suffering a broken foot weeks after the draft. He missed a few months of the 2024-25 season because of a fractured pelvis, returning to play a key role in the Thunder's championship run. Holmgren earned first-team All-Defensive and third-team All-NBA honors last season, when he averaged 17.1 points, 8.9 rebounds and 1.9 blocks per game. The Thunder also said Wallace underwent surgery Friday and will be reevaluated before the end of the regular season. Williams underwent surgery Wednesday and will also be reevaluated before the end of the season, the Thunder previously said. Agbaji, the No. 14 pick in the 2022 draft, has averaged 7.2 points and 2.7 rebounds in 263 games, including 108 starts. He was waived by the New York Knicks in final roster cuts earlier this month.

stories.title: Warriors’ comeback vs Lakers unprecedented: ‘25, it’s the new 12′
stories.summary: No team in the NBA has ever erased a 25-point deficit by halftime or ended up winning by as much as the Warriors did over the Lakers.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO — It was deader than dead inside Chase Center after the first quarter Friday night, a fitting graveyard-like atmosphere on the eve of Halloween. A motivated Luka Doncic exploded for 21 points and the Lakers built a 23-point lead by the time Steve Kerr gathered his team on the Warriors’ bench between periods. They should have been spooked. It was about the worst 12 minutes of basketball Golden State had played this season. It appeared Kerr’s squad was headed for a second rout in 10 days at the hands of the Lakers. Then, everything flipped. Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry (30) smiles during an NBA Cup basketball game against the Los Angeles Lakers on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, in San Francisco. AP Photo/Justine Willard Austin Reaves got to the foul line on the Lakers’ first possession of the second quarter, extending their advantage to 25 points, 40-15, and that’s as wide as it would get. De’Anthony Melton scored the next seven points, and Golden State went on to come all the way back — and then some — for a convincing 112-95 win over Doncic and the Lakers . From the end of the first-quarter timeout on, the Warriors outscored Los Angeles 97-57. “I don’t think I got too upset. I was trying to stay poised,” Kerr said. “We couldn’t have played any worse, and they knew it. I didn’t need to tell them. I just said it’s a long game. “I don’t think I said anything about the modern NBA — I didn’t say anything to our players — but what I would [say] is 25, it’s the new 12. These games happen nightly in the league.” Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr shouts to get an official’s attention during a game against the Los Angeles Lakers in San Francisco on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026. Getty Images They don’t usually happen quite like this, though. In fact, the Warriors’ Jekyll-and-Hyde act produced a kind of game that had never been seen in the NBA, at least not in recent history. As poor as the opening period went for the Warriors, the second was just as bad for JJ Redick’s squad. By halftime, Golden State had erased the entire deficit to pull even at 53. It was the first time since the NBA started tracking play-by-play (in 1996-97) that a team had trailed by 25 or more in the first half and come back to even the score at halftime. The final 17-point margin of victory was the largest by any team that has trailed by 25 or more. “These games are wild,” Kerr said. “With the pace and the 3-point shooting, there are just these wild swings. You just have to stay with it.” While Kerr kept his cool after the disastrous first quarter, the assistants in the second row of the Warriors’ bench let the players have it. They committed 10 turnovers, double their number of made baskets, and seemed to be rattled by Doncic’s furor in his rematch with Yaxel Lendeborg. Anthony Vereen was the “lead voice” in calling out the Warriors players, Steph Curry said. Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry (30) shoots a 3-point basket against the Los Angeles Lakers in an NBA Cup basketball game, Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026. AP Photo/Justine Willard “You need that kind of fire to see how we’re gonna respond,” Curry said. And respond, they did. After coughing up the ball 10 times in 12 minutes, they turned it over only six times over the remaining 36. Only one team ended up with a positive assist-to-turnover ratio, and it wasn’t the one that jumped to the early 25-point lead. The Lakers ended up turning the ball over five more times than Golden State (20-15) and assisting on 13 fewer buckets (31-18). Brandin Podziemski of the Golden State Warriors points toward the Los Angeles Lakers bench at Chase Center in San Francisco, Friday, Oct. 30, 2026. Getty Images “Everything went wrong,” Kerr said of the first quarter. “It was just a weird quarter. It was not anything strategy related. We didn’t change anything after the first quarter. “Sometimes when you come back off a weeklong road trip and you have a day off, no shootaround, that first few minutes can be a little rough. That would be my excuse for tonight.” In addition to his 21 first-quarter points, Doncic looked unstoppable as a playmaker, dishing out five assists. He finished with 37 points to best Curry’s 31, but he didn’t set up another Lakers bucket for the rest of the game. “Luka had an unbelievable first quarter,” Curry said. “He looked very determined coming into tonight. Our offense got stagnant. Turnovers the first four or five minutes were deflating. “We had a lot of chatter at the end of the first quarter, and it was kind of cool to see the second unit — just the overall execution on both ends in the second quarter.”

stories.title: LeBron James on 5-1 76ers: 'I'm more than happy I made the decision to come here'
stories.summary: LeBron had 20 points and the dagger putback Friday as the 76ers beat the Knicks. Again.
stories.detailText: "Best game all around. He's been good, but that was his best game for sure." That was how coach Nick Nurse described LeBron's performance Friday night, via Noah Levick at NBC Sports Philadelphia . LeBron finished with 20 points, nine rebounds and eight assists, leading Philadelphia past New York — again! — on Friday night, but the numbers don't tell the story. He was the glue that made the entire 76ers project fit together, and when it mattered most he had the dagger putback. LEBRON DAGGER ️ pic.twitter.com/QP9p5z3dXl — NBA on Prime (@NBAonPrime) October 31, 2026 It's just six games, but LeBron said he couldn't be happier with his offseason decision to come to Philadelphia, via the Associated Press. "I'm having a great time," James said. "I love what we're bringing to the table every night. I love our competitive spirit. Guys show up to work. Guys are ready to work hard. It's a fun group, too. I'm like a big-ass kid, to be completely honest. These guys are great to be around and I'm more than happy I made the decision to come here." LeBron got plenty of help as his friend Tyrese Maxey dropped 27 points, and Anfernee Simons came off the bench and hit five 3-pointers on his way to 21 points. That covered for a rough night from Joel Embiid on the offensive end, where he shot 3-for-12, but he still had seven assists and seven rebounds. Jalen Brunson started making plays in the fourth quarter, as he so often does, and the Knicks walked down an 11-point 76ers lead in the fourth to make it a game late, and he finished with 24 points. Karl-Anthony Towns had 22 points and 12 rebounds. However, when it mattered most, LeBron settled the 76ers down. That's what he brings most to the table, Maxey told NBC Sports Philadelphia . "Leadership. Calming presence. He helped get a lot of rebounds. He'd help get the ball and calm it down. He was great. At the end of the day, it's LeBron James. At the end of the day, he can do stuff like he did tonight, getting a couple of big buckets." His leadership has Philadelphia off to a 5-1 start — and LeBron is healthy and happy. That's all the 76ers can hope for this early in the season.

stories.title: JJ Redick is confused about the lack of consistency in flopping technicals
stories.summary: The Lakers keep ending up on the wrong end of flopping technical decisions and don’t understand why.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 30: Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers complains after he thought he got fouled by Brandin Podziemski #2 of the Golden State Warriors at Chase Center on October 30, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming into the season, the point of emphasis that drew the most attention was the added focus on push-offs by offensive players . However, through the opening week-and-a-half of the season, it’s been the theatrics on the other side of the ball that have been punished. Flopping technical fouls have been the flavor of the week for the Lakers. Starting with a post-game fine levied on Ziaire Williams last weekend, the purple and gold have become very familiar with the new point of emphasis. After being the victim of Scott Foster’s antics that featured a trio of flopping technicals in quick succession against the Blazers, Tony Brothers strolled into San Francisco and created his own drama, including the most erroneous flopping call yet. Jarred Vanderbilt is hit with a flopping technical, as Al Horford drives on him and unintentionally steps on him, on the way (with replays) pic.twitter.com/zeQjF0nyCg — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) October 31, 2026 Later on in the fourth quarter, another sequence drew the ire of the Lakers as Brandin Podziemski attempted to draw a foul with a particularly theatrical sequence. But not only was no common foul called, but neither was a technical foul for flopping. austin reaves; brandon podziemski; lakers vs warriors pic.twitter.com/69fSQyOYVS — ◇ (@F0RGIAT0) October 31, 2026 It’s all added up to some head scratching for the Lakers and head coach JJ Redick, who spoke about the flopping technicals after Friday’s loss to the Warriors . “We all recognize we want the offensive players to stop fouling,” Redick said, referencing himself and fellow coaches around the league. “All of our flopping fouls have been defensively. The reality for the officials, each crew is so different and what they interpret is so different. I think the consistency – the explanation I got for the Podziemski play was there was contact. But if you look at our flopping fouls that we’ve been called for defensively, there’s been contact. Whether or not there’s contact is irrelevant. “We’re looking for something theatrical and extra. So if that’s not a foul and then throwing yourself back, I would assume that, to me that’s kind of the definition of flopping. Again, that was the explanation I got was there was contact. But, again, there was contact on a push off when Ziaire moves his hands back because they called it an offensive foul. So, there was contact but I guess the consistency, we’re still searching for it.” The problem with these flopping technicals is that not only will different officials consider different things flopping, as Redick said, but it’s also never going to be called consistently. The Lakers went multiple games before a flopping technical was given to them, then saw it called in a flurry of games. There is no standard flopping motion as there is with other violations. For example, you know when a player goes over the back or when a defender reaches in for a steal and hits a wrist or arm. With flopping, though, it can take so many forms and, thus, some officials may view some movements as flops and others not as much. In theory, it’d be great to get flopping out of the league. But right now, they’re not addressing the issue that existed but, instead, are creating a new one. You can follow Jacob on Twitter at @JacobRude or on Bluesky at @jacobrude.bsky.social .

stories.title: Steph Curry drops Luka Doncic — and finds his joy
stories.summary: SAN FRANCISCO — Steph Curry dribbled through his legs and then jabbed hard to his left, sending Luka Doncic flying onto the ground. Curry stepped back, seemingly stunned that his...
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO — Steph Curry dribbled through his legs and then jabbed hard to his left, sending Luka Doncic flying onto the ground. Curry stepped back, seemingly stunned that his closest defender was on his butt. He swished a 3-pointer. Curry put both hands over his head. He shimmied his shoulders. It was poetry. It was vintage Curry. It was the embodiment of joy. “I didn’t expect it to get that nasty,” Curry said in his postgame interview with Amazon Prime Video after the Warriors’ 112-95 win over the Lakers . “It was one of those [moments] you kind of got to keep your composure. I remember James Harden used to do the shimmy to get himself open back in the day. I don’t know. I haven’t been that open in a long time.” Doncic was still on the ground as Curry elevated midway through the third quarter. The league’s leading scorer was dropped by the greatest shooter of all time . Curry is still him . The Warriors have now won three games in a row, including turning a 25-point deficit into a 17-point lead on Friday. They’re finding their groove. They’re fueled by Curry’s joy and a sprinkle of something new: his palpable acceptance that this isn’t going to last forever. He’s engaging the crowd. He’s putting on a show. He’s savoring this. “I just love this game,” Curry said. “All my mannerisms are all over the place because I’m just having fun. In those moments, especially at this stage of your career, you’re just appreciative of the ability to keep playing at this level. And I want that joy to continue until I’m done.” We’re seeing glimmers of what Warriors basketball was at its peak. It comes in spurts, such as in last season’s play-in win over the Clippers when Curry went into a flow state, scoring 35 points, and Draymond Green transformed into a full-blown defensive beast, holding Kawhi Leonard to two points in the fourth quarter. Curry breaking Doncic’s ankles was another example of that. It was a master at his craft making us all shake our heads and smile. It was the type of moment that will be memorialized. When Curry is having fun, we’re having fun. And when he’s having fun, the Warriors are dangerous. Steph Curry warms up before a season-opening game between the Golden State Warriors and the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles, Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. London Entertainment They’ve turned things around following a sluggish 0-3 start to the season. Against the Lakers, Curry had 31 points, including going 8-for-14 from deep. That performance followed a 44-point, eight-rebound, six-assist stunner from Curry in the Warriors’ 119-114 win over the Timberwolves on Wednesday. Curry is the master of the show. But the team is getting contributions from everywhere. Yaxel Lendeborg is putting on a Rookie of the Year campaign, though he had a quiet six points and one rebound in his much-hyped showdown against Doncic following their trash talk in the teams’ season opener on Oct. 21. On a night in which Lendeborg was a nonfactor, the Warriors’ bench outscored the Lakers’ reserves, 50-7. … Making things even more interesting: Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody will return in a few months. Could the Warriors actually be good? Everyone had counted them out, something Curry rejected. When a reporter asked Curry on Warriors media day about the team not being expected to make the playoffs, he balked. “That’s how bad? Not make the playoffs? It went from championship to —.” Curry then put his hands up and uttered a few lighthearted “damns” as he walked out of the room. At the time, his reaction was funny. But, hey, maybe we erroneously overlooked the Warriors. Maybe we erroneously overlooked him. Steph Curry warms up before a season opener between the Golden State Warriors and the Los Angeles Lakers in Los Angeles on Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026. London Entertainment The runner’s knee that caused the 38-year-old to miss 27 straight games last season is looking bionic. He’s shining. He’s refusing to accept the reality that he’s aging or the narrative that the league’s modern-day dynasty that won four championships in eight years from 2015-2022 is flailing. When Curry is on, he’s still the best show in the league. Lendeborg didn’t hesitate when asked to describe Curry’s play on Friday. “The stuff he was shooting and making, it was just like what are you doing?” Lendeborg said. “How are you even doing that? The people on the bench call him a sicko. I don’t even know. It was astonishing. Dude doesn’t get tired. He dribbles like that all day and doesn’t get tired.” Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry, right, confers with head coach Steve Kerr in the second half of an NBA basketball game in Denver, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski Lendeborg — and everyone else who watches Curry — is regularly left stunned. It has been that way for the last decade. And even though he’s about to turn 39, that hasn’t changed. Curry dropping Doncic amid a 42-point swing was epic. It was instant basketball lore. It was the league’s legendary shooter teaching its current superstar a history lesson on national television. It was Curry reminding everyone of his greatness.

stories.title: Lakers’ Austin Reaves has blunt 4-word response to turnover woes
stories.summary: Austin Reaves was a big part of the Lakers' turnover struggles against the Warriors.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO — A lot went wrong for the Lakers to blow their 25-point lead to the Warriors on Friday night at Chase Center. Cold shooting from the Lakers. Steph Curry’s highlight-reel-worthy plays, including eight 3-pointers. And turnovers. Austin Reaves (15) once again struggled with taking care of the ball. NBAE via Getty Images Lots of turnovers. The Lakers committed a season-high 22 turnovers against the Warriors, sparking easier shots in transition against a defense that wasn’t set. The biggest culprit of the Lakers’ lack of ball security was star guard Austin Reaves. He finished with eight turnovers against the Warriors, the same number of turnovers he had in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers . Reaves didn’t hold back when it came to assessing his performance. “I was terrible again,” he said postgame. “That’s it.” Austin Reaves was honest about his performance. NBAE via Getty Images Reaves entered Friday coming off his worst game of the season so far. The sixth-year guard had 16 points on 6-of-16 shooting to go with eight turnovers in Wednesday’s road win over the Clippers. Against the Warriors, he didn’t perform as poorly but came close. Reaves had 21 points on 9-of-19 shooting to go with five assists and four rebounds, but he once again struggled with taking care of the ball. Austin Reaves will need to handle two-on-the-ball defensive coverages better. Getty Images Reaves struggled early with the Warriors’ defensive pressure and strategies, recording six of his turnovers in the first half. His three turnovers in the second quarter, which the Warriors won 38-15 to tie the game at 53 after the Lakers led 40-15, were especially costly. “Just bad — we were bad,” Reaves said. “That first group that started the second was bad. And like I said, it starts with me, so I’ll be better.” For Reaves, getting better means handling the more defensive coverages with more poise. And for the team, it looks like building chemistry over the regular season will help avoid situations they found themselves in that led to turnovers on Friday. “I mean, it’s real, but it doesn’t give that second unit an excuse to be pretty terrible,” Reaves said. “And that starts with me. And I’ll watch the film, try to be better. You got to learn on the fly and pick up things quickly. But as I said, I have to be better to start that.”

stories.title: One Possession: The secret to unlocking hugs from Joe Mazzulla
stories.summary: Payton Pritchard earned a rare hug from Joe Mazzulla during Friday's win over the Bulls.
stories.detailText: One Possession: The secret to unlocking hugs from Joe Mazzulla originally appeared on NBC Sports Boston It’s been a sometimes confusing week for the Boston Celtics. Derrick White looked baffled when he got MVP chants Tuesday night inside TD Garden while shooting free throws against the Brooklyn Nets. Payton Pritchard came to the sideline on Friday night after two dominating first-half stretches against the Chicago Bulls and found a smiling Joe Mazzulla waiting with a hug. Smiles and hugs? From Mazzulla? It turns out the secret is pretty simple. Respond to the coach’s challenges, and you might just get an in-game squeeze. View this post on Instagram Pritchard grabbed only three rebounds, but one in particular jumped out to us during his first-quarter takeover. Pritchard tracked a long rebound and launched himself between both teammate Hugo Gonzalez and Chicago’s super springy Matas Buzelis to secure the ball. Pritchard then broke out the other way in transition, accelerated past one Bulls defender, and took a bump from another while delivering an and-one layup that had Boston out front 40-21. For the second time in a week, Pritchard had delivered a double-digit quarter against the Bulls. He finished the first quarter with 12 points on 4-of-4 shooting and added 2 steals on the defensive end. Pritchard went on to finish with a team-high 30 points on 9-of-17 shooting over 34:45. “Joe challenged me and I feel like, in the first four games, my defensive activity and my rebounding has been poor,” said Pritchard. “So [Mazzulla was] challenging me to to step up in that area and I think the hug was for me to be like doing that and him being thankful I’m doing it … We’ve been through a lot together and so it’s just great to keep it going, and then I stepped up to the challenge in that area.” View this post on Instagram Despite his size, Pritchard has routinely ranked as one of the best rebounders on the offensive glass for his position. He’s been a bit more middle of the pack among point guards on the defensive glass, but that rate has plummeted to a career-low 5.4 percent to start the 2026-27 season, or nearly half his career rate. That one tough rebound in traffic on Friday night was a reminder of how being active on the defensive glass can help fuel Pritchard’s overall output. What’s more, Pritchard was credited with defending a team-high 14 shot attempts against the Bulls, who shot just 35.7 percent when he was the primary defender, or 7.9 percent below expected output. View this post on Instagram “I think in tonight’s game you saw the absolute best version of him,” said Mazzulla. “Now, that takes a ton of energy — not going to be able to do that every single night. But the sky is the limit for him. And, as we continue to grow as a team and he continues to grow as a player, being able to be a complete player on both ends of the floor really helps us take it to a different level.” While further gushing about Pritchard, Mazzulla added: “I like pushing him.” For one night, all that pushing led to an embrace.

stories.title: Sixers try to keep it rolling in Charlotte with both teams on short rest
stories.summary: Less than 24 hours after tipping off against the Knicks, the Sixers will be in Charlotte to take on the Hornets.
stories.detailText: There is never any rest for the weary in the NBA. After a thrilling 98-93 win over New York , their second over the defending champions on this young season, the Sixers are back in action less than 24 hours later on the road against the Charlotte Hornets. It’s reasonable to expect a much different looking Sixers team for this game. After missing last night’s Knicks win with patellar tendinopathy in his left knee, it’s hard to imagine Jaylen Brown will be available to play. Joel Embiid and LeBron James both played in the front end against the Knicks, so it feels likely neither of them will be available either. Charlotte is still waiting on Kon Knueppel, Coby White and Grant Williams to make their season debuts. They could also have more guys out of the lineup having also played Friday. They lost to the Wizards in Washington, falling to 3-3 on the season. The Sixers went 2-1 against the Hornets last season but with the Sixers adding Brown and James and the Hornets trading Lamelo Ball, these teams are way too different to take anything from that. In a very small sample size and without one of their best players, the Hornets are currently profiling as a drastically different team. At the time of writing, they are 30th in points scored per 100 possessions, a number skewed by their 79-point performance in Washington. They’re 10th in points allowed, according to Cleaning the Glass. They’ve won all three of their games by seven points or less. Two of their three losses have been by 15 points or more. Fresh off a contract extension, Brandon Miller is averaging 25.6 points per game this season but is just shooting 39% from the field. Even potentially without LeBron and Brown, the Sixers seem as equipped to handle talented scoring wings as ever. Dean Wade is coming off a phenomenal night guarding OG Anunoby. Assuming Embiid doesn’t play, Adem Bona and whoever else fills the center minutes could have their hands full with Naz Reid. As the starting center on his new team, Reid has averaged 17 points per game shooting 43% from the field and a scalding 42% from three on seven attempts so far this season. Ryan Kalkbrenner, their backup, could also give them problems just by being a long seven-foot-one. This should be a fast paced one, with the Sixers also wanting to fly up and down the floor with their guards running the show. VJ Edgecombe should be in line for his first real high usage game of the season. He’s been great as a glue guy but has only scored over 15 points once this season. The only thing he hasn’t done well so far is shoot the ball. He’s shooting just 29% from three this season, but hit a massive triple from the top of the key to help seal that win against the Knicks. Even against a team like Charlotte, the Sixers will need big games from both members of VJ Maxx, or potentially another heater from Anfernee Simons to sweep this back-to-back. It will take a village to fill center minutes for the time being, assuming Embiid isn’t available. Game Details When: Saturday, October 31, 6:00 pm ET Where: Spectrum Center, Charlotte, NC Watch: NBCSP/PCK-PHI Radio: 97.5 The Fanatic Follow: @LibertyBallers

(Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Sixers beat the Knicks on Friday… …meaning they are 2-0 in the head-to-head matchup. That’s it, that’s all it means. No parade down Broad Street. Here’s what we heard coming out of Cheesesteak Arena. "We're competitive when we need to be & that's why all the games that we're in we have a chance down the stretch. Trying to make sure we continue to do the little things throughout the course of the game is going to be huge because we're not doing that right now" -Mike Brown pic.twitter.com/EedUgrhbHY — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 31, 2026 Mike Brown On losing to the 76ers in the NBA Cup: “I don’t look it as a statement game. It’s the next game in front of us. Obviously, it’s a [NBA] Cup game and you always want to push yourself to have an opportunity to try and win something. This means taking a step toward that goal. “But I just want to get a little better every time we play. These guys really hurt us in transition last game. Our transition defense right now stinks. But it’s gotten a little better. Tonight, it will be tested. Obviously Jaylen is not playing and he’s one of the best in transition. You look at little things and you hope to get better at the little things while getting a win.” On the Knicks allowing Philadelphia to attack the paint too easily: “They were getting in our paint left and right, right and left, and it was really, really easy doing it.” On the Knicks forcing difficult plays instead of executing simple offense: “It’s been going on all year. Like, we’re trying to hit a home run every time we get the ball. And we have to hit singles. We can’t hit a home run. We gotta hit singles offensively and then if our play breaks down, we have to move. There’s too many times where we have too many guys trying to iso and the other four guys sitting there and staring at the ball a whole possession.” On the Knicks improving their turnover management in the second half: “We did a better job with our turnovers (in the second half). But more importantly, we reacted better when we turned the ball over and we had five turnovers for six points (against).” On the Knicks failing to maintain their focus throughout an entire game: “Against a good team on the road, if you let go of those things in a half, you’re in trouble. And so somehow some way we have to be cognizant of doing this stuff for 48 minutes, which we’re not doing right now. “Tonight it was the first half and it was almost like [we thought] we’re just gonna show up and go hoop and not do the little things that we need to do to go get a win.” On the importance of executing the fundamentals consistently: “It’s a little thing here, a little thing there, a little thing there. … We’re competitive when we need to be and that’s why all of our games that we’re in we have a chance down the stretch, but trying to make sure we continue to do the little things throughout the course of the game is gonna be huge for us because we’re not doing it right now.” On LeBron James making decisive plays against the Knicks: “[LeBron’s] a great player, and when you have a great player out there, with his ability, he’s gonna make plays, and he made big plays down the stretch. It’s the NBA, and it’s not surprising when a guy like Maxey or LeBron or Jalen makes a big play. You just hope that it doesn’t come down to that all the time.” On Ernie Johnson’s retirement announcement and his impact on NBA coverage: “I’d like to give a quick shoutout to Ernie Johnson. I don’t know him well. Obviously I know him from the TV. I try not to watch a lot of basketball shows because it gets me too high or gets me too low. But their show is one that I always get good laughs at. “Just from afar, Ernie seems like he’s a big time human being. And the little bit I know about his story, it’s fascinating. He will be sorely missed, not only from the fans out there and other media members, but I know from a coaching standpoint too in keeping everything light and enjoyable and all that other stuff. “So I hope you have a heck of a year, Ernie. We’re gonna all miss you, but thanks for doing what you do to make people smile everyday.” "There's been plenty of times we learned from being down what we can do. In that same game we made adjustments. I think we played decent in the second half. Took care of the ball better, played better defense. You've got to put a full 48 minutes together" – Jalen Brunson pic.twitter.com/jw2Koojswi — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 31, 2026 Jalen Brunson On the Knicks’ careless turnovers and hesitant decision-making: “Just a little careless. And sometimes it can be us being hesitant as well, wanting to make the right play, but they’re also not trying to turn over, and then it’s just a little late to our decision-making. It could be a lot of things, but obviously, we got to clean it up.” On Josh Hart’s fatigue excuse six games into the season: “Josh said he feels the fatigue? Well, Josh is old as s–t, so.” On the Knicks needing to learn from their losses and stop relying on comebacks: “I’ve said in the past that it’s always important to learn from wins. Obviously, you learn from losses, as well. There have been plenty of times that we’ve learned from being down. In those same games, we’ve made adjustments to where we weren’t down anymore and came back and won the game. Obviously, we have to understand what we need to do. It’s starting the game that way. I think that has to be our biggest point of emphasis going forward. “I thought we played decent in the second half, took care of the ball better, played better defense, but we have to put a full 48 minutes together.” "All I can think about is we're now six games in. We haven't shown our best. We haven't played our best. We've got to find a way to be that magical team we were last year at a more consistent pace. Lightning don't strike twice. We've got to be that team now" – Karl-Anthony Towns pic.twitter.com/eu2kkztOD5 — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 31, 2026 Karl-Anthony Towns On the Knicks lacking energy against Philadelphia: “Today we played like a team that was on the end of a road trip. We gotta find that gear. We gotta find that energy. “We picked up the pace in the second half, but what makes this team special is doing it for 48 minutes. We didn’t do that tonight. We put ourselves in a bad spot, and give credit to the team over there. They hit the shots when they needed to. We just got to execute at a higher level.” On escaping the Knicks’ offensive struggles too late against the 76ers: “I thought we did a great job in that fourth quarter of finding that gear, like you said, just kind of getting out of the quicksand. To do that puts us in a position where you gotta make some magic happen, and we just didn’t have enough magic tonight.” On the challenge of facing LeBron James and the 76ers: “They’re a great team. Obviously, you have arguably the greatest player of all time. We’ve got to bring our best. We’ve got to execute at a high level. And we’ve got to continue to use these games as a learning experience.” "We all feel the fatigue. We've got to fight through it. 6 games in, but we have to find a way to make sure we get our bodies ready to play every day" – Josh Hart pic.twitter.com/mYadahO50F — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 31, 2026 Josh Hart On the Knicks’ stagnant offense and lack of movement: “It’s a new year. I think we’re trying to work our way into the season. But I think the flow’s tougher. Sometimes the ball is stagnant, I think that’s a little bit from fatigue and not a mental thing. You know what the other team is doing, and physically you’re trying to get your body to get to that point. So I think that that’s part of it. We got to be more deliberate with cuts and movements. And taking care of the ball.” On the Knicks feeling fatigued after playing three games in four nights: “We all feel the fatigue. So we got to fight through it. Six games in. So we got to find a way to make sure we get our bodies ready to play every day. I think mentally we’re there. We just gotta find it physically.” On the Knicks needing to execute more consistently: “We gotta find a way to execute better. And do that continuously.” On why the Knicks keep falling behind by double digits before attempting comebacks: “I wish I could tell you that one. If I could tell you that one, and the reason why, then maybe it would stop happening. I think we all have a great will to win. I think sometimes it takes us a little longer to find a game, whether that’s the flow, fatigue, whatever it is. “We have to do a better job of finding the game early, making it easy and then not relying on double-digit comebacks because it’s taxing.” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse says LeBron James has been good so far all season, but tonight was his best game. pic.twitter.com/0YWemLAudP — Dave Uram (@MrUram) October 31, 2026 Nick Nurse On LeBron James’ performance against the Knicks: “He’s been good, but tonight, I thought that was his best game for sure. I thought he was good all the way through tonight. I thought he got some downhill stuff. He used his size and knocked them around a little bit for some layups. I thought he obviously pushed the ball and got us organized. I thought he was a little quicker to make some decisions to shoot the 3-ball as well. And then, he obviously made those couple of big plays down the stretch.” Amar'e Stoudemire on why #Knicks have gotten off to a slow start after championship season: "I think what we most have to look at is that when you win a championship, especially in New York, you have all these different opportunities off the court that take place. You're filming… — DJ Siddiqi (@DJSiddiqi) October 29, 2026 Amar’e Stoudemire On how New York’s off-court opportunities can distract players after winning a championship: “When you win a championship, especially in New York, you have all these different opportunities off the court that take place. You’re filming commercials, you’re having these different shows, you’re doing these different things. All these events are happening. “You’ve got to try to narrow it back down and lock in on basketball because playing in New York, you can get a little bit taken away from the sport with all the activities that go along with being in New York City. But you have to now try to narrow it down back to basketball. Key in, lock in on basketball. Make it the main priority and build out from there.” On why the Knicks deserved to celebrate their championship throughout the offseason: “That’s normal. That’s a part of human nature, man. You win a championship for the New York Knicks. You kidding me? After 53 years, you gotta enjoy that. You will never be the first one to win it after 53 years ever again. “So that energy, you have to capitalize on it. It’s just a matter of now being able to kind of channel that and now focus on basketball and lock in a little bit more.” On whether the Knicks’ slow start is concerning: “I’m not concerned. When you are the champions, man, every target is at your back. Every team’s gunning for you, so it’s tough to kind of get off to a great start the following year. I’m not concerned. I think it’s a matter of just kind of locking in and focusing a little bit more, and they’ll be okay.” CURRY YOU ARE THE GREATEST PG EVER pic.twitter.com/83m34YREe0 — wok (@wokdior) October 31, 2026

stories.title: Warriors make absurd NBA shot-clock era history in huge comeback win over Lakers
stories.summary: The Golden State Warriors turned a 25-point first-half deficit into a 17-point win over the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night at Chase Center.
stories.detailText: Warriors make absurd NBA shot-clock era history in huge comeback win over Lakers originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area The Warriors’ 112-95 win over the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night at Chase Center was one of the wildest rides in modern NBA history. In their third consecutive win, the Warriors erased a 25-point first-half deficit and prevailed by 17, setting the NBA’s shot-clock era (1954) record for the largest margin of victory after trailing by 20-plus points in the first quarter (h/t to the Associated Press’ Josh Dubow). Biggest margin of victory in shot-clock era for team that trailed by 20+ points at end of 1st quarter: Warriors 112-95 vs Lakers, tonight (down 23) Warriors 124-110 vs Bulls, 3/4/1976 (down 23) Timberwolves 131-118 vs Pacers, 12/21/2007 (down 20) — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) October 31, 2026 The 1975-76 Warriors, led by Rick Barry, Phil Smith and Jamaal Wilkes, previously held the record with a 14-point win over the Chicago Bulls on March 4, 1976. On Friday, Luka Doncic was on a mission to send a message to Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, and the Lakers star did that, dropping 21 first-quarter points to pace Los Angeles to a staggering 38-15 lead after the first 12 minutes. But the Warriors flipped the script — literally — in the second quarter, responding with their own 38-15 quarter, sending the game to halftime tied at 53. In the second half, Steph Curry and the Warriors clamped down on the Lakers, outscoring them 59-42 to run away with a blowout win, an outcome that seemed impossible after the first quarter. “Luka had an unbelievable first quarter,” Curry told reporters after the game. “He looked very determined coming into the night. Our offense got stagnant, turnovers the first four or five minutes were just deflating. But we had a lot of chatter at the end of the first quarter about how we were supposed to respond, and it was kind of cool to see the second unit, and just the overall execution on both ends in the second quarter. “We turned them over a good amount, got in transition, got better spacing so we could move the ball and get open threes, and a couple shots started to go to flip the score like we did at the half and hold them under 95 after a 38-point first quarter is pretty impressive from everybody.” The Warriors look to keep the momentum going when they host the 1-4 LA Clippers on Sunday at Chase Center. Dub Nation’s blood pressure might appreciate an easier path to victory. Download and follow the Dubs Talk Podcast

stories.title: Sixers down Embiid and James to end back-to-back in Charlotte
stories.summary: The Sixers will be undermanned for their game Saturday night against the Hornets.
stories.detailText: Sixers down Embiid and James to end back-to-back in Charlotte originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers will be down at least two stars Saturday night when they finish their back-to-back. The team listed both Joel Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management) and LeBron James (low back sciatica management) as out for its matchup with the Hornets at Spectrum Center. Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) are also sidelined. Both Embiid and James also sat out one leg of the 5-1 Sixers’ first back-to-back. Embiid has averaged 35.2 minutes through five games. The seven-time All-Star’s career high is 34.6 during his 2022-23 MVP season. James had his best performance so far as a Sixer in the team’s win Friday night over the Knicks , scoring 20 points and coming one rebound and two assists short of a triple-double. The Sixers listed three players as questionable on their initial afternoon injury report in Jaylen Brown, Jabari Walker and Tacko Fall. Brown and Walker each have a knee injury officially classified as “left patellar tendinopathy.” Brown missed his first game as a Sixer on Friday. Fall has a left quadriceps injury. The big man on a two-way contract hasn’t yet been available in either the preseason or regular season, but he’s been nearing a green light to play. The 3-3 Hornets won’t have Kon Knueppel (left hamstring strain), Coby White (left calf strain) and Grant Williams (right hamstring strain).

stories.summary: Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving and Dusty May talk about what the Mavericks did well in the team’s 116-111 win over the Rockets
stories.detailText: DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 30: Kevin Durant #7 of the Houston Rockets and Kyrie Irving #11 of the Dallas Mavericks looks on during the game during the Emirates NBA Cup on October 30, 2026 at American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas.
