Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Garrett Ellwood/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Dallas Mavericks (4-2) topped the previously undefeated Houston Rockets (5-1) on Friday, 116-111 , at American Airlines Center, and, boy, was it a thing to watch. If this is what Mavericks fans are in for this season, buckle up — it’s going to be a thrill ride in 2026-27. Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving wrecked the Rockets in the fourth quarter, scoring 25 of their combined 68 points down the stretch as the Mavericks completed the comeback. Here is what head coach Dusty May, as well as the dynamic duo had to say in their postgame press conference. Dusty May Opening statement I don’t know the rest of the league well enough other than film, but I can’t imagine that there’s too many teams tougher than the Rockets. I thought, especially in the second half, when the shots are going in, and you’re in a rhythm, and things are going well, you can match the other team’s physicality and intensity. When they aren’t going in, some teams just can’t do it. I thought late, some guys that weren’t having their best game stepped up and grabbed big rebounds. Dusty May says this Mavs team feels special to him pic.twitter.com/zDVkQyvjmh — MavsHighlights (@MavsHighlights) October 31, 2026 Obviously, our two guys, they just made play after play, but so many other possessions jump out. Gafford’s blocks at the rim were huge. P.J.’s rebounds in traffic late. I think he got three in the last three minutes, and we needed all of them. Obviously, Zacc in the second half. Caleb Martin, back the last couple games from injury, has shown what he is — a winning player. On to the next. What has clicked since for the team since the season-opening blowout loss to the Rockets? I thought our effort was good. There didn’t seem to be any leak-outs — guys that weren’t in the fight. I thought we were in the fight. We took care of the ball better. We had 17 [turnovers], and that’s still better than game one. But it seemed like most of our turnovers, other than a couple of just, we had numbers and we just kind of threw it to the wrong guy. A lot of them seem to be dead-ball turnovers, which is an improvement. This is Houston. They’re tough to play against. On Kyrie Irving’s build-up back into form: If you just saw how much he puts into this game, and that factors into being on a young team, and bringing it every day and helping the group find solutions to problems and doing it in the manner in which he does it, I mean, it’s incredible. That’s why his stat line, 35 [points], 9 [assists], and four [rebounds], that looks great. It’s obviously impressive, but his leadership and his grace with his teammates is even more impressive to me. How rare is it for a 19-year-old to do the things that Cooper Flagg is doing, especially at the end of games? What a problem, where you’re in a pickle where two guys like that just have it going, and you just got to kind of rotate between putting the ball in each other’s hands, and knowing that they’re going to make the plays. So obviously, what a luxury for us. And once again, they both trust their teammates. When Houston put two on the ball, and they were determined to take it out of their hands, they continued to trust and trust and trust. And then those reps and that experience, those guys handled it better. I think we hit more, Gaff more in the short roll than we have every, all the including preseason, the games we played Houston combined. And that’s a sign of finding, you know, having some answers, but also the trust factor that Coop and Kyrie have with their teammates. What are you most proud of with this team? We look like a team that, you know, obviously, when things weren’t going well, you know, when I watch these games just to see how our bench is about each other. And I want to shout out Dereck Lively. He’s a big part of that. His energy is contagious, and he’s got such a positive spirit to him. But yeah, just the fact that we look like a group trying to find a way to win together, no matter what it looks like. They’re playing the game in front of them, and they’re doing it as a unit. How did Daniel Gafford rebound after getting hurt late? I thought he was — early on — he was having his worst game of the year. And he’s been really good for us. And the second half was just another level. I mean, when you’re able to block those attempts at the rim, usually it starts a break going the other way, but those are energizing, momentum-changing plays. And off the top of my head, I can remember several. And then to step up and knock down the free throws at the biggest moment. Just made winning play after winning play. On Irving’s big second half: I mean, don’t overcomplicate it. Just get the right matchup on him and let him go to work. And like I said, when he’s playing that efficiently, shooting the ball, and he’s finding his teammates, and those are leading to hockey assists or regular assists, it’s just, you know, don’t overcomplicate it. How much does Flagg factor into how to get Irving the space he needs to operate? When you go back and look at it, one of them would screen the other one. One of them would cut to get some attention off the other one. And also, it’s just tough to go when you’re in a tight game with probably six minutes left of a one-possession game, for one guy to do it over and over and over and over and over. It’s taxing. And then the defense that they have to play and exert the energy they have to exert on the other end — for those guys to be able to share that load and have two guys who just are closers like they are — there’s several layers to it. But, you know, that makes you feel good, very confident going into close games. On the moment team president Masai Ujiri and May shared in the tunnel after the game: Masai Ujiri and Dusty May share a moment after the Mavericks’ big win over the Rockets. pic.twitter.com/xOiKjwyWZy — Noah Weber (@noahweber00) October 31, 2026 You know, obviously I have a ton of respect for Masai, and he’s been a great sounding board, and I’ve probably asked him too many questions just as I learned — as myself and staff were trying to learn this organization and whatnot. And so it was just a little joke that I made, but just very, very appreciative of the team that front office has put together. We’re deep, we’re young, we have great character more than anything else. I haven’t been around very many teams, but this group feels like a very, very special group of human beings first, and they’re working like crazy to get better at basketball. What makes character so important, and how doe sit align with winning teams? You know, I don’t want to go into all that, but the teams that, whether things are going well or whether they’re going poorly, simply get to the next thing, the next practice, the next game, the next possession, those are usually the teams that are standing longer than they probably should have otherwise. What went into the decision of not activating Naji Marshall? He hasn’t practiced. … It looks like he’s dropped weight, he hasn’t practiced yet and we thought if we can get through this one without Naji, then he’s got two days to get his body back right, get his conditioning and then be ready to play well Monday. We needed him tonight. I mean, it was a tough decision not to throw him out there, but we just thought for our team and for him, just give it until Monday. He was down with the illness. Cooper Flagg How much has your confidence grown in the 75 games you’ve now played in your NBA career? Cooper Flagg tonight 🔥🔥🔥🔥🔥 33 PTS 9 REB 6 AST 2 STL 1 BLK 13/19 FG pic.twitter.com/tyabyN4EPc — Shabazz 💫 (@ShowCaseShabazz) October 31, 2026 It’s grown a ton. Just being confident, getting to my spots and living with the result. That’s something I talked about last year, and it’s going to continue to be a thing. All the great players are able to just get to their spots and raise up and knock them down. So that’s all I’m trying to do — just get to my spots, and we’ll live with outcome. Have you talked to Irving about those moments where you just know the ball is going in when it leaves your hand? I talked to him a lot about it last year. Trying to learn from him — the mental side, but I think more and more, as we’ve gone to this year, just being able to see it in person and on the court from him and being able to learn from the experience has been really cool, too. How would you describe what you and Irving were able to accomplish on the floor together? I thought, like I said, just playing off each other really well. He was able to go on runs and be a very vocal leader with the ball in his hands. I was able to come in, be able to contribute in a very similar way, and it kind of just made the game easier for each other, and I thought that was really, really good. How comforting is it to have another co-star on the roster? That was great. We have a lot of stars. Guys are being stars in their roles, and I think that’s what we’re seeing. We’ve started to get a couple wins here early. It’s just guys really just sacrificing and being a star in their role. Guys like Zacc, P.J., Gaff, those guys are all stars in their roles, and they’re vital to our success, but it’s felt great to have [Irving] out there, someone that puts the ball in the basket better than the best of them. On teammates’ performances in the win: Gaff … never backed down from the challenge. He’s always there protecting the paint, getting the rebounds. I mean, that’s a big team. So I think just down the stretch, him blocking out and helping us grab some rebounds was huge. PJ, same thing, just a physical defender. He’ll knock down his open shots, but I think just the work he did, rebounding the ball down the stretch for us was huge. Caleb, I thought, was really big tonight, and what he did defensively and just rebounding. Zacc has been really good all year — just getting into [passing] lanes, getting deflections, steals, blocks, being all over the place. So yeah, those guys, they’re vital to our success, for sure. Where have you grown the most as a player since last season? I just think the confidence is continuing to grow and grow, and I feel like I’m just more comfortable at this point. Having a year of learning all my peers, earning their respect is a big thing for me. And I feel like at this point, it feels comfortable. And I know where I want to get to and what I want to do get there. What were you able to take from playing in so many clutch games a year ago? Just being comfortable. You need those game experiences. There’s nothing like it. You know, the crowd loud, everybody excited, coming down. There’s a lot of mental things that you can do to affect a game like that down the stretch. So just learn from that last year, and try to put it to use. What has Dereck Lively’s energy been like on the bench as he continues to recuperate? It’s been great. Live has been one of the loudest people on the bench every single night. And you can tell he’s really just itching to get back out there. But just what he’s done from the sidelines and the energy and the positivity that he’s brought to our team has been incredible. And he’s definitely been a big part. What about [Lively’s] game makes you excited for him to join the active roster? I think in just the small time that I was able to play with Live last year — his defensive versatility. I mean, a lot like Gaff, just holding down the paint. Being a really big presence, shot blocker, and a lob threat. So that’s a really good screen. So he sees the game at a high level too. So I think a lot of people underrate that about Live. And I’m excited to get back out there with him eventually. And people will be able to see how he sees the game and can affect it. What’s the key to you and [Irving] divvying things up? Is it based on the opposing defense? I mean, it’s not a perfect formula. And obviously, I think we’re still working out a lot of the kinks and figuring out how we can help each other best. And there’s been a lot of moments where we realize that we can help each other more out there on the court together. So there’s been a lot of learning experiences. And it’s been a pleasure to be able to play alongside him and learn from him out there. But yeah, I think there’s still more and more that we can do to help each other, alleviate some pressure, and continue to just learn how to play together. And make it easier for one another. Kyrie Irving First question muffled: Kyrie: 35 PTS (26 in 2H) 9 AST Coop: 33 PTS (18 in 2H) 6 AST The dynamic duo leads the @dallasmavs to 1-0 in West Group A! pic.twitter.com/6GfHzLBDu7 — NBA (@NBA) October 31, 2026 Which part? The good stuff, or stuff at halftime where it looks like we probably didn’t give our best effort because of who was in the lineup? And it’s just art of war kind of thing. Just psychologically when Alperen Sengun’s out and then Reed’s out, we have a whole game plan for them. And then we kind of take our foot off the gas pedal a little bit. So we just had to readjust. It’s a human element of it. But when you’re in competition, you can’t do that. And I feel like we picked it up after halftime and just had a few conversations with some guys. And we all agreed. We weren’t playing our best basketball. And in order to be considered the best in this league, you got to bring the energy every single night. You got to bring the physicality. And you’re going against an undefeated team that’s very confident, playing well. They’ve had a few games down the stretch where they’ve been able to pull out some tough wins. And I think tonight was our time to prove that against them. Preseason went how it went. We’ve been talking about how we’re playing them eight times in the first 20 games. But I think it’s just a great learning experience for us. To be able to go down the stretch and just win. What was the difference for you in scoring 26 of your 35 points in the second half? I think my communication and also my aggression and just starting the third quarter off at a very high level. Especially pushing in transition and getting the ball above half court, over half court before 21 seconds or 20 seconds, whether it was a miss or a make. And just paying attention to the details on the defensive end. They’re always looking to catch you sleeping. Amen’s always looking to catch you sleeping on the offensive glass while he’s crashing. KD’s always looking to be around the basketball when they’re kind of going through their possessions where they haven’t scored in a minute. And Ime does a great job of letting Fred just free flow into the offense as well as Marcus Smart. And just learning throughout the minutes and possessions through the games. Just some of their cues that they’re mentioning to each other. Some of their nonverbal communication — their eyes, their eye fakes. They continue to press you and press you and press you and wear you down. I felt like we had to kind of take that energy and reverse it on them. And just make sure they played on their heels and they were trying to get up quick shots. And we were just playing with the offensive verve that we needed to. What does tonight mean after the long injury absence? It was incredibly special. I’m obviously, you know, it’s the in-season tournament. You know, depending on which team you play against, some teams are taking it serious, some teams aren’t. But I think there’s a good kind of pressure environment to have early in the season where it wasn’t just about me playing well or Cooper playing well. We really needed to have possessions where they mattered. And guys were, you know, making the right plays or weren’t making the right plays, and we just had to learn from it. So we’re going to be in a lot of games like this, you know, down the stretch throughout the year. I don’t know when, but hopefully we can get some 20-point wins where we don’t have to go into it. But when we’re going into some, you know, end-of-game things, we got to be able to be sharp, be focused. And I felt like we were able to do that. And the guys were really leaning on me for some emotional support, some verbal communication. And I feel like I offered that. And I also just was confident within the game. Like, we just had to break over that hump. We were within seven points, and it was five points, and it was 10, and it was nine. It’s just — we had to break that seal off. And I felt like we did it with our defense and also just having smart possessions on the offensive end. On the chemistry between Flagg and himself down the stretch: It’s beautiful to watch, you know, whether the ball’s in my hands or the ball’s in his hands. You know, it’s just in terms of our selection of shots. He’s going to get into the paint. I’m going to be an outside perimeter threat. He can be an outside perimeter threat. I can get in the paint. But I think overall, our teammates trusting us to be able to make the right plays. And then, you know, honestly, just in reality, since just having a teenager out there, you know, making these tough shots and getting and-ones and being as clutch as anyone I’ve seen, it’s just amazing to be a part of. And it does take some pressure off of me to be able to make plays down the stretch. And I think that’s what makes it beautiful to watch and experience. And we’re still growing. I think he said it best. You know, we still have a level that we want to get to, a higher level. And we’re going to continue to push each other to do so. And we obviously know the external chatter as well about the 15-year age gap and what we can accomplish and how we’re going to mesh. And I think we kind of throw that out the window and just really focus on what we can control, which is our effort and how we treat each other. You know, he’s a very diverse threat. I’m a very diverse threat. And we just play off each other well. Evaluating Flagg’s development 75 games into his NBA career: Yeah, I always speak on his competitive nature. It’s very rare. I mean, you obviously have guys that are very talented, do a lot of great things athletically. But that competitive nature and that drive to want to be the best, to want to win ball games, to want to do the little things — that has to come from and within. And I think he exudes it. Sometimes you look at him, he looks tired, and he makes an outstanding play, a block, or he hits a tough layup or he throws a lob. It just helps settle us win. And whenever we’re out there on the offensive perimeter, we’re able to identify what our match-ups are and be smart about it. So I think his IQ and his competitive nature has put him in this spot today. And I think the pressure really bothers him. He has a great supporting cast around him, including myself, a veteran, where he could look to me, and there hasn’t been too many concepts or too many things in games I haven’t seen. So I know he’s relatively new to us. He’s no longer a rookie, so we don’t have to treat him like that. But we give him his respect as he continues to earn it. And that’s what the NBA is about. At what point in your career did the clutch shot become kind of an unconscious thing? I mean, it probably for me started in fifth grade, to be honest with you. I think that my dad put the ball in my hands very young, and I had to earn my teammates’ trust. And I think on every team, obviously I play different roles, but when everybody’s looking at you to shoot the shots or looking to another teammate to shoot the shots, and you’ve earned it. And you got to earn it in practice. You got to earn it in the way you work on your game, and then you got to show it in the big-time moments. And you got to deal with the emotional up and down of making missing. That’s it. So the clutch gene can be developed, or it’s innate, or both. On Risacher’s impact on the team: Yeah. I mean, I think the practices that we’ve had, the preseason that we had, I can’t necessarily use the word surprised like everyone else in terms of his effort and what he’s been able to do. He’s right on track in terms of being a young player in this league and establishing himself and really proving himself. And it’s tough being a number one pick and having the franchise pressure on you, and then now being in a new environment and having to develop or accept a new role. And I think he’s done it fabulously. And when you’re around other talented players and high-level players, you’re going to have to adjust and you’re going to have to adapt. He started in the starting lineup in preseason, and he’s adjusted to coming off the bench, first guy off the bench at times, which helps us. So I think the selfless approach that he’s taken has been very mature of him. But we’re going to need him to do other things. And depending on health, God willing, we all stay healthy. But if we don’t, then there’s going to be times where he’s going to be in the starting lineup, and he’s going to be asked to do more. And I think he’ll be able to step up to the plate. But right now in his role, he’s superstar in it, just being able to get the stocks, be able to push and transition. He’s the fastest player on the court during every single game. It’s beautiful to watch somebody like that, just like a gazelle going up and down the court and beating bigs, beating wings. And it helps us a lot when we’re trying to make a push. And those little plays that don’t slip on the stats sheet is what he’s become great at. On hitting shots over bigger defenders like Jabari Smith Jr.: I mean, it’s a great feeling when you know the work translates into the games. It was the first four games, five games. I really felt like my body has been in a good place. But there’s more that I can get out of my instincts. There’s more that I can unlock in my game. There’s more of an attack mindset. There’ll be times I’m out in the perimeter. I’m not really cutting, or I’m not really active. And I just don’t want to be stagnant on those possessions. And even when the possessions change from offense to defense, I really want to be able to push myself. And that just comes with reps and comes with rhythm and also making the choice to get out and run despite just maybe some of the mental fatigue or physical fatigue. And just not thinking about like, hey, how do I feel right now? It just should be about playing tonight. And just playing the possessions out. And that’s probably the first game out of the last four where I felt like I was just playing out the basketball game by possessions, IQ, without thinking about like, all right, how does my leg feel, or how do I feel physically? How do you feel after playing 35 minutes? I feel great. It was great to build up to this moment. I think thinking about how we were talking about the minutes restriction in the first game versus Houston and how it was kind of controlling my internal frustration. But I trust our coaching staff. I trust our medical staff in being able to develop a great dialogue and getting to this point and just takes patience. And I’m going to enjoy it, but also give myself a lot of grace as I’m continuing to get better throughout the season. On May’s coaching style: Well, I’ll keep it short because I don’t want any of these other coaches around the league to get jealous. But he’s a great guy, in terms of, I’m not trying to give away all his sauce and stuff like that. He’s a great guy in terms of being able to identify what skill sets he has on his team. He’s done that very early. He’s very confrontational in terms of what he wants out of you. And I think it helps in terms of just establishing our concepts and what we need to do game-to-game and preparation-wise. He’s a big preparation guy, which I appreciate as well. What does the NBA Cup mean to the team? I mean, we have a chance to bring, or have an opportunity to bring home a trophy in the first part of the season. And we know who’s in our group. And we know what’s in front of us. And we just got taken one game at a time. But I think when I first answered this question a few years ago about the in-season tournament. I wasn’t that excited about it, just like other veterans or other guys in the league. But I think I understand the concept now in terms of what it means for a fandom of basketball and also for the franchise. And just getting your legs up underneath you. I think we saw the Knicks last year going against the San Antonio Spurs. And we saw that in the finals. So there is some correlation to playing well early in the season and picking it up and then being able to have some early success, and that lead to [big things] later down the line.

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Gary Dineen/NBAE via Getty Images). | NBAE via Getty Images The Milwaukee Bucks host the Cleveland Cavaliers tonight in the final game of the Bucks’ three-game home stand, which saw them notch their first victory of the season against the Pacers before getting blown out by the Rockets. Tonight, Donovan Mitchell and the Cavs roll into town fresh off a road loss in Atlanta, so they’ll be extra hungry. The Cavaliers are 3-2 so far this season, having gone unbeaten at home and winless on the road, a streak they hope ends tonight. The Task Ahead Despite being undefeated at home, the Cavaliers’ season has been mixed so far. Their offense is posting 114.1 points per 100 possessions, ranking 10th in the NBA. The defense, however, allows 113.4 points per 100 possessions, ranking 16th. This inability to gel on both ends is partly due to the offseason roster shake-up and, most notably, the need to integrate Peyton Watson. While Watson obviously isn’t solely responsible for the entire team’s misgivings, the Cavs still haven’t got what they paid for. Against Minnesota on Monday, Watson recorded four blocks and three steals in a close OT win over the Timberwolves. Great! He also went 0/5 from three and is shooting just 14.3% from deep this season. In Cleveland’s loss to Atlanta, Watson recorded just four points. This underscores how crucial Watson’s success will be for Cleveland’s success this season. Therefore, a key matchup in this game will rest on the wings. If Watson can impose his will on Jaime Jaquez Jr. and use his athleticism to close out effectively and defend, the Bucks may find themselves on the wrong end of another blowout. Jaquez, though, has shown some considerable skill this year putting the ball on the ground to create when he needs to—and at his best, can even get elite defenders to bite on his fake-outs—so it will be a battle between IQ and athleticism on the wings. Another factor to watch is how well both teams move the ball. The Cavaliers and Bucks both rank in the bottom-10 in assist percentage this year, so whoever finds their rhythm first can take control early. Injury Report Bucks: Clean injury report. Rockets: Nae’Qwan Tomlin: out (low back pain) Jaylon Tyson: out (ankle sprain) Meleek Thomas: questionable (ankle inflammation) Player to Watch Jarrett Allen is off to yet another highly efficient and effective start to the season. His usage rate is down, but his true shooting and rim protection numbers are up. Allen’s scoring opportunities, however, have decreased this year due to Cleveland’s lack of wing creation. If the Cavs can get more perimeter production from their wings, it would draw defenders out and allow Allen to feast in the paint. Myles Turner, for all of his flaws, has been solid defensively, so if anyone can pressure Allen at the rim, it is him. However, if the Bucks’ bigs are pulled out of the paint to guard on the perimeter, it could spell a big night for Allen down low. stories.title: LeBron James shines vs. Knicks in 'his best game' with 76ers
stories.summary: LeBron James rescued Philadelphia late against the Knicks in what coach Nick Nurse called his best game as a Sixer.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- A step-back 3-pointer from Jalen Brunson erased what had been an 11-point fourth-quarter lead for the 76ers on Friday night, sending the Knicks -heavy crowd at Xfinity Mobile Arena into a frenzy. But the Sixers had an answer: LeBron James . On the next possession, James backed down Knicks forward OG Anunoby before taking two dribbles to the middle of the floor and fading away for a jumper to help the Sixers reclaim the lead. A minute later, James made a putback layup to put the Sixers up five points with 11.9 seconds remaining, a finishing dagger in what was ultimately a 98-93 NBA Cup win that moved them to 5-1 on the season. "He's been good, but that was his best game for sure," Philadelphia coach Nick Nurse said of James. Sixers guard Tyrese Maxey called James a "calming presence" in late-game situations. James' leadership has been a large reason why all five of their wins have come in clutch time (final five minutes, score within five points), including two over a Knicks team that had won six straight in the series entering the season, including a second-round playoff sweep en route to the NBA title. "At the end of the day, he's LeBron James," Maxey said. "So it's just like he can do stuff like he did tonight, a couple of big buckets." It was the first 20-point game of James' Sixers career as he finished with 20 points, nine rebounds and eight assists. He has scored 20 or more points in 68 games since turning 40, more than every other player age 40 or older in NBA history combined (67). He also tied Hall of Fame center Kareem Abdul-Jabbar as the fifth-oldest player (41 years, 304 days) in NBA history with a 20-point game. James said that while he doesn't think about those feats, he is surprised at how long he has been able to play at such a high level. "I'm definitely not going to lie to you and say that I knew it would be 24 years, that's for damn sure," he said. While Nurse called it James' best game as a Sixer, his play did fluctuate throughout. With forward Jaylen Brown out with a left patellar injury, James came out aggressive with 12 points on nine shots in the first half. But he disappeared in the third quarter with just one shot attempt and two points, both on free throws. He shined in the fourth quarter, scoring six points, more than half of which were game-saving. "I'm having a great time," James said. "... I'm a big-ass kid, to be completely honest, but these guys are great to be around, and I'm more than happy that I made the decision to come here." The Sixers play at the Charlotte Hornets on Saturday.

stories.title: Bucks Reacts Survey Results: Fans are down with—not on—Jenkins’ rotations
stories.summary: Despite the record, fans are mostly thrilled with who Taylor Jenkins is playing—and who he isn’t.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 16: Taylor Jenkins the head coach of the Milwaukee Bucks gives instructions to Ryan Rollins #13 against the Indiana Pacers at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on October 16, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Roughly two weeks into the NBA season, Milwaukee Bucks fans are liking what they’re seeing, despite the team’s losing record. In fact, fans are more than just happy. Jenkins jubilation Overall, 72% of fans are full of praise for Jenkins, citing his boldness, his ability to assign roles, and his ad-lib cooking (that is, his ability to make the best out of what he’s got) as key qualities: Punitive concerns Despite the overall positivity, not all Bucks fans are smelling the roses, with 21% only somewhat happy with Jenkins’ rotations, 6% not happy, and 1% thinking they stink. Within these subsections, a prominent concern lingers regarding a certain Gary Trent Jr. and how not playing him might look to Adam Silver and the powers that be amidst the ongoing cap circumvention probe: Showcasing “talent” Finally, some sections of the fanbase feel Jenkins must be showcasing Myles Turner. After all, his play hasn’t warranted the starting gig—or all those “empty-calorie” minutes that have come with it: Yes, after saying and doing all the right things off the court during the offseason, Turner has been bad on it to start the season—and not in the 1987 top-of-the-charts kind of way. For more on that, be sure to catch this week’s Winners & Sinners , coming soon. With rotation contentment high but wins low, the question thus begs: how long can this relationship coexist? That is, how long will it be until the losing takes its toll? Here’s hoping that becomes a moot point.

stories.title: Who Are The Minnesota Timberwolves: What The First Five Games Tell Us
stories.summary: The Wolves have shown their high ceiling and their injured floor through five games. What else can we glean?
stories.detailText: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 28: LaMelo Ball #1 of the Minnesota Timberwolves looks on during the game against the Golden State Warriors on October 28, 2026 at Target Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by David Sherman/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves find themselves with a 3-2 record through the first five games of the NBA season, including wins over Eastern Conference playoff teams in the Miami Heat, Orlando Magic, and Toronto Raptors, while suffering an overtime loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers and falling short against the Golden State Warriors in their last contest due to a 44-point outburst from Stephen Curry. The Timberwolves are featuring a different look with a new roster featuring LaMelo Ball at point guard after shipping out Julius Randle in the off-season. With the early returns of the new roster still uncertain, the big question is: “Who are the Minnesota Timberwolves?” STEPH GIVING LAMELO & THE TIMBERWOLVES PROBLEMS 🤯 FIVE THREES IN THE SECOND QUARTER ALONE 🍿 pic.twitter.com/J7NacEstZa — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) October 29, 2026 It’s been a battle-tested season for the Wolves early. Facing the new-look Heat with Giannis Antetokounmpo to open the season was a performance for the ages, filled with optimism to see how Ball would impact an already dynamic offense. The Wolves did not disappoint as superstar guard Anthony Edwards dropped in a whopping 45 points on 55.2 percent shooting from the floor and a scorching 52.9 percent from beyond the arc on 17 attempts. He complemented that with 10 rebounds and two steals with the team’s second-best plus-minus at +25. LaMelo Ball helped play spoiler against the Heat as well in his 28 minutes, pouring in an efficient 21 points while hitting five of his 13 attempts from deep alongside six assists to take down the Heat 131-106. The next two games followed a similar path as the Wolves dominated the Magic on the road in Orlando, defeating them by 22 points, and then crushed the Raptors at home in Minneapolis (albeit without Kawhi) by 23 and handcuffed Scottie Barnes to an abysmal 0-12 shooting night . They followed those performances with a disappointing overtime loss to the Cavs , largely in part due to a lackluster performance from Rudy Gobert, and a loss to the Golden State Warriors due to a slow start and Curry doing Curry things and Edwards being out due to a lingering right knee injury. The Timberwolves have shown they are capable of high-level offensive outbursts and stifling defensive performances. How have they gotten there? According to NBA.com , the Wolves have the fourth-best offense in the league on a points-per-game basis, averaging 120.4 over the five contests. This places them behind the Portland Trail Blazers, Los Angeles Lakers, and the Houston Rockets, who are first, second, and third in the league, respectively. They are also posting an offensive rating of 114.8 for the eighth-best mark in the league while shooting 47.3 percent from the floor and 38.4 percent from distance. A large reason for this top-10 offense has been the dominance from Anthony Edwards , notching 33 points per game on 48.1 percent shooting overall and 40 percent from three on 11.3 attempts per game. TJ Shannon Jr. has also been a positive mark this season as he’s gotten a longer leash, averaging 14.2 points per game on 40 percent from deep, while other staples such as Ayo Dosunmu and Jaden McDaniels have continued to play well and keep building on impressive playoff runs from last season. Newcomer Jonathan Kuminga has also been a bright spot, shooting a blistering 47.6 percent from three on 4.2 attempts per game. They’re all doing this collectively without marksman Donte DiVincenzo as he continues to rehab an Achilles tear he suffered against the Nuggets in the first round of the playoffs last year. The defense, which is anchored by four-time Defensive Player of the Year Rudy Gobert, is second best in the NBA according to defensive rating, posting a 102.5 mark , right behind the Raptors with a league-best 97.9. This puts together an impressive 12.4 net rating, which is the fourth-best mark in the league. They’re also limiting opponents to 45.3 percent overall and 33.6 percent from three-point range, which positions them in the upper half of the league. Putting it all together, both through the eye test and the objective numbers, everyone should know who the Timberwolves are: a team that can dominate on both ends of the floor while maintaining both a very high floor and a championship-level ceiling, all while figuring out another roster that was shuffled yet again. all of us rn 😂😂 https://t.co/0OVn8m3lMd pic.twitter.com/Dtx1oFIHIS — Minnesota Timberwolves (@Timberwolves) October 26, 2026 In a small sample size, the Wolves have shown they have what it takes. However, they will need to continue to tread water in a loaded Western Conference as Edwards will be out for at least the next two months after it was announced he underwent a successful right knee arthroscopic surgery to clear out some debris. It will be an interesting stretch without Ant for an extended period of time, and the Wolves will need to cement their identity and playstyle a lot quicker than imagined. We know who the Wolves are through the first five games, but who will they be without Ant for now, and will they have the same dominance that’s been displayed when he returns?

(Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second time this week, the Wolves fly from Minnesota to take on a rested team on the tail end of a back-to-back. This is their fifth game in seven nights. They are down their A1 player in Anthony Edwards but have found a way to win without him. To add to their win total in San Antonio will take a full team effort with what they have left. Game Info Who: Minnesota Timberwolves (4-2) vs. San Antonio Spurs (3-2) When: Saturday, October 31st at 7:00 PM CT Where: Target Center – Minneapolis, MN Local TV: DAZN-MN, DAZN-SAS Radio: 830 WCCO Conference Semi-Finals Rematch This is the first matchup between the Wolves and Spurs since their playoff bout this past May. The Spurs would continue past Minnesota on their march to the final round where they were summarily spanked by the New York Knicks (thanks Karl). Karl-Anthony Towns L of New York Knicks vies with Victor Wembanyama of San Antonio Spurs during the final game 5 between New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs at the 2025-2026 NBA basketball game in San Antonio, the United States, June 13, 2026. (Photo by Wu Xiaoling/Xinhua via Getty Images) The Wolves President of Basketball Operations Tim Connelly saw that the path through the Western Conference now curved through either Oklahoma City or San Antonio and their brand of swarming, hyper-athletic, in your jersey, perimeter defense. The Spurs being anchored by an All-Defense big man near the hoop. As he did when building the Wolves to take on Nikola Jokic and the Denver Nuggets , he made a big trade that sent out precious draft capital and beloved players. The new vision was built around LaMelo Ball. An All-Star pass first point guard who can bend defenses in the half-court with either his passing or shooting. In the past the Spurs tore up the hobbled Wolves by sending two defenders at Anthony Edwards who had little means of releasing the pressure in ways that punctured the defense. This left Victor Wembanyama clear to sit back and ward off the paint. The Wolves size that they had used to stifle the Nuggets was chop blocked. Unfortunately we will not get to see Connelly’s full grand vision in action take on one of the very teams he built it for. As Edwards recovers from his successful arthroscopic surgery, the Wolves will instead have to contend with a team off to their own rocky start. The Spurs are 3-2 with victories over the Dallas Mavericks without Cooper Flagg, the Sacramento Kings, and the Utah Jazz in overtime. At this writing they are middle of the league in shooting the basketball (tied at 18th in true shooting percentage at 56.2%), while boasting a top ten defense. The Wolves have played well thus far against teams that lack consistent three point threats. Should the Spurs find some of their post-season form and hit from outside, it could get ugly fast. Double Vision San Antonio could employ the same defense they used in the playoffs against the Antless Wolves. Melo is a more capable ball handler and passer than Edwards and is better able to diagnose where to deliver the ball. What he is not, is someone who can handle a full night of physical bullying. Especially after playing a game 24 hours earlier. Sending two players in any combination of Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, or Devin Vassell could rattle Ball’s cage enough to turn the Wolves over. I expect the Spurs will try to rough up Melo and frustrate him. If Rudy tries to screen him open, Wemby will hedge just enough to prevent the deep shot knowing he can catch up to anyone in the play diving to the rim. The rest of the Wolves will need to move well off the ball and keep the Spurs guessing where and when Melo might look to release the defensive pressure. Centre Bleu! Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Combing the standing reach of Rudy Gobert (9’7”), Joan Beringer (9’3”), and Wemby (somewhere between 9’7”-9’10”) we could run nearly one third of court tip to toe with French center. Outside of Luke Kornet minutes, the entirety of this game figures to see two of those three on the court at all times protecting the rim. Where Wemby has more outside game than either Rudy or Joan, all of them do their best work on offense closer to the basket. Thankfully Rudy got back in the scoring column against the Clippers. As the elder homme d’État, he’ll need to bide his time to score against Wemby, collecting offensive rebounds when Big Vic is pulled far enough away from the rim and slamming them home before the defense can recover. As the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, Wembanyama stalks around the basket like Jack Skellington on the hunt for a new holiday. What the Wolves, specifically Terrance Shannon Jr., discovered last year in the post-season, is that you have to go at the man in the middle. This will not always reap rewards, but if Minnesota can get past their perimeter defender they need to go at Victor and force him to make a play. The more the Wolves can make Wemby exert himself on one end, the more he will lack on the other end by the fourth quarter. On the second night of a back-to-back, it is a big ask for Minnesota, but Wemby is at his worst in the fourth. Serviceable last year, Kornet has yet to find a rhythm this season. Sample size theatre but something to keep an eye on. Ball and Jonathan Kuminga will feed off that energy and look to help their teammates looking to steal back their pride. Minnesota’s outside shots fall and they take the lead weathering a few surges by the Spurs. It gets close in the third but by the fourth, Wemby is spent and the Wolves tuck San Antonio into bed early, leaving a night light on for fear of the big bad wolf. Happy Howloween! This summer, the league unveiled the full group stage schedule for this year's in-season tournament, with action taking place every Friday from Oct. 30 to Nov. 27 and on special Cup nights during Thanksgiving week (Nov. 24-25). After the New York Knicks became the first team to win the NBA Cup and Finals in the same season, can Jalen Brunson & Co. keep their championship run going? They'll have plenty of competition, specifically within the star-studded East Group B. Here's what you need to know about the in-season tournament, now in its fourth year. Jump to a section: Schedule | Groups | FAQ Warriors 112, Lakers 95 After leading the Warriors by 34 points through three quarters on opening night and by 23 after the first quarter Friday, the Lakers looked ready to coast to their fifth win in six games this season. So how did Golden State end up winning 112-95? Luka Doncic poured in 21 points in the opening frame, his 10th quarter scoring at least 20 points since joining the Lakers -- tied with Kobe Bryant for the most by any Laker since 2000. And the Lakers' defense seemingly carried over whatever it found when it put the clamps on the LA Clippers in Wednesday's win by limiting Golden State to 15 points on 5-for-22 shooting in the first 12 minutes. Two of those five makes came from Stephen Curry , however. And he kept hitting shots as the game went on. Three more makes in the second quarter, three more in the third and another three in the fourth to finish with 31 points on 11-for-23 shooting. Meanwhile, Doncic slowed down. After shooting 7 for 12 in the first quarter, he went 5-for-15 the rest of the way. By the end of the night, Curry moved past Dominique Wilkins for No. 18 on the NBA's all-time scoring list, and the highlights dried up for the Lakers, particularly when coach JJ Redick went to his bench. Golden State's reserves outscored Los Angeles' second unit by a staggering 47-7. Just more than a week since the Lakers and Warriors started the season headed in opposite directions, the gap between the two teams is tougher to discern. Golden State has won three straight, and Jimmy Butler is working to come back from a torn ACL by midseason. The Lakers have lost two out of three despite most of their core being available, except for youngsters Ziaire Williams , Adou Thiero and Cameron Carr . Friday showed that a game can drastically change from one quarter to the next, just as a team's season can flip from one week to the next. -- Dave McMenamin 76ers 98, Knicks 93 Philadelphia was up by eight early in the second quarter of their eventual 98-93 win in Friday's NBA Cup opener against New York when Sixers rookie guard Labaron Philon Jr . received a pass from Tyrese Maxey and advanced the ball past half court. Philon quickly found backup center Adem Bona on the left wing, then Bona pitched it back to Maxey standing near the Cup logo in the tipoff circle and went to set a back screen on the Knicks' rangy defender Mikal Bridges , hoping to free Maxey when the Sixers scorer put it on the floor. Then a dizzying sequence commenced, with the ball moving around the court like a marble in the "Mouse Trap" board game. Maxey passed it back to Philon, who had replaced Bona on the wing; Philon pump-faked, drove middle and passed to an open Anfernee Simons on the right wing. Simons swung it to Dean Wade in the right corner. Wade drove the paint and kicked it back to Simons above the 3-point line. Simons drove right and flipped the ball behind his back to Wade, who replaced him at the top of the key. Wade swung it to the left wing to Maxey. Maxey faked a pass to Philon in the left corner and then used his dribble to attack the lane and throw down a one-handed dunk with the shot clock ticking below four seconds. Nine passes. All five Sixers touched the ball. And the action started and ended with Maxey. As Philadelphia continues to establish exactly what team it is going to become this season with so many new players to mesh and outside expectations to manage, the 76ers showed Friday some of the tenants they have already come to rely on: Maxey is going to drive the offense. His 27 points led both teams, and he has scored 26 or more in all six of Philly's games. The Sixers are going to play unselfishly. They had 26 assists on 37 made baskets with LeBron James (20 points) and VJ Edgecombe (13 points) contributing big-time late buckets after Jalen Brunson briefly gave the Knicks the lead in the fourth. They are going to play defense, no matter who is in the lineup. Jaylen Brown , perhaps their best wing defender, was ruled out Friday because of left patellar tendinopathy. Philly still held New York to 41% shooting overall and 32% from 3. While a few of the Sixers' early wins have come because of furious second-half efforts -- turning things around against New York and Cleveland in the third quarter and needing a 39-21 burst in the fourth against Indiana to prevail Wednesday -- this was a more complete game. Semifinals Dec. 11: Championship NBA Cup FAQ: Everything to know What is the format? NBA commissioner Adam Silver has had a longstanding fascination with European soccer. Establishing an in-season cup competition within the NBA schedule came from soccer leagues having both a regular-season title, won by the team with the most points over the full year, and a separate tournament (or, in some leagues, multiple tournaments) that runs concurrently with the league season. In England, for example, there are the various divisions -- led by the Premier League -- and also the FA Cup competition. But unlike those European leagues, which play their cup competitions outside of their league schedules, the NBA Cup is built in to the regular-season slate. The 30 NBA teams are split into six five-team groups -- three featuring Eastern Conference teams and three comprising Western Conference teams -- with each team then playing one game against the other four in its group. The winner of each group, plus the team with the best record among the non-group winners, advances to the knockout stage of the competition. How will this impact the regular-season schedule and standings? Typically, the NBA sends out a full 82-game schedule in mid-August. Now, the league sends out only 80 games and leaves a gap of roughly a week to fill in later, depending on how the group stage of the NBA Cup plays out. The two teams from the East and West that lose in the quarterfinals will play their 82nd game against each other. Meanwhile, the 22 teams that fail to qualify for the knockout rounds will have their final two games scheduled -- one at home and one on the road against others eliminated in the group stage. The teams that reach the NBA Cup final will actually play 83 games -- though the championship game won't count toward the standings or any statistical markers. The four teams that reach the semifinals will have completed their 82 games and won't need any other games added to their schedule. Any team that makes it to the semifinals will have that game moved later in the schedule to avoid back-to-back games. The NBA made this change in an effort to avoid having empty days on the calendar while attempting to minimize back-to-backs for all teams as much as possible. Where are the semifinals and final being played? In a shift from previous tournaments, the quarterfinals and semifinals will be played at home sites. The Dec. 11 title game, meanwhile, will move from Las Vegas to the storied Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis. NBA commissioner Adam Silver previously said the league was searching for "storied college arenas" to play host to the Cup final. (No venue has been announced for 2027.) Why does the NBA Cup include regular-season games? Before its launch, one of the main questions surrounding the in-season tournament was why any team would be incentivized to compete in it. The NBA ensured teams will be motivated by making every game part of the season and, as in-conference matchups, potentially important to playoff tiebreakers. If this had been set up like the cup tournaments in European soccer, there would have been nothing stopping NBA teams from opting out by sitting their top players for extra rest. Which teams make up the groups? To create the groups, the NBA put the 15 teams in each conference into five pots, separated by their finish last season. Pot 1 included the teams that finished in the top three in the regular-season standings, Nos. 4-6 in the standings went into Pot 2, Nos. 7-9 into Pot 3, Nos. 10-12 into Pot 4 and Nos. 13-15 into Pot 5. As a result, the following groups were drawn: East Group A Detroit Pistons Toronto Raptors Orlando Magic Milwaukee Bucks Brooklyn Nets East Group B New York Knicks Cleveland Cavaliers Philadelphia 76ers Miami Heat Indiana Pacers East Group C Boston Celtics Atlanta Hawks Charlotte Hornets Chicago Bulls Washington Wizards West Group A Denver Nuggets Houston Rockets Phoenix Suns Dallas Mavericks Utah Jazz West Group B Oklahoma City Thunder Minnesota Timberwolves LA Clippers New Orleans Pelicans Memphis Grizzlies West Group C San Antonio Spurs Los Angeles Lakers Portland Trail Blazers Golden State Warriors Sacramento Kings Does one group stand out the most from the others? East Group B is a monster. All five teams -- defending NBA Cup and Finals champion New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Miami and Indiana -- are among the favorites to win the conference in 2026-27. The group stage will also feature reunion games for LeBron James , when the 76ers face the Cavs and Heat. And after guard Tyrese Haliburton missed the entire 2025-26 season while rehabbing a torn Achilles, the Pacers will be back among the East elite and hungry to reach the title game in Indianapolis. What do players get for winning? In 2023, the first year the tournament was held, the players on the winning team received $500,000 each and the runners-up got $200,000. The losing players of the semifinals each got $100,000, and those ousted in the quarterfinals got $50,000. Now, in each subsequent year, the prizes will be slightly higher, as a result of negotiated raises year over year to keep pace with increases in the salary cap and basketball-related income as part of the most recent collective bargaining agreement between the NBA and the National Basketball Players Association. Will anyone earn individual honors for their play in NBA Cup games? There will be an MVP award, as well as an all-tournament team. Will this have any impact on the playoffs? Not beyond the games counting in the regular-season standings (and toward tiebreakers). The only playoff impact comes from the wins and losses accrued throughout the tournament. Though there was debate among league insiders about guaranteeing a playoff berth for winning the tournament, ultimately that idea (or any other to further incentivize teams) was not enacted. Why is it called the Emirates NBA Cup? The league struck a sponsorship deal with Emirates, the Dubai-based airline, to sponsor the tournament after its initial run. The NBA said last year that it went with the most basic titles for both the tournament and its trophy -- the "in-season tournament" and "NBA Cup" -- as a way to introduce the concept to fans. However, using such nondescript names had another clear advantage: It gave the league a blank slate in case it sold the naming rights for the tournament and cup to a sponsor and avoided the complications that could arise by naming them after someone (for example, late NBA commissioner David Stern, one possibility that had been floated before the tournament was officially unveiled). stories.title: Of eight use of helmet infractions in Week 7, only Cam Skattebo was flagged
stories.summary: The fine imposed on Giants running back Cam Skattebo for illegal use of the helmet was not a rarity.
stories.detailText: The fine imposed on Giants running back Cam Skattebo for illegal use of the helmet was not a rarity. The flag thrown in real time for it was. Of eight fines levied by the NFL for use-of-helmet violations in Week 7, only Skattebo's came with a flag. The league fined Skattebo $7,073. The seven players fined but not flagged were: Bears cornerback Clark Phillips ($11,550); Broncos safety Brandon Jones ($23,882); Broncos Alex Singleton ($47,662); Lions safety Brian Branch ($23,882); Colts cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt ($7,791); Steelers receiver Brandon Smith ($4,916); and 49ers running back Jordan James ($6,194). The fines increase as the violations repeat. For Singleton, who was fined $23,882 for illegal use of the helmet, it was the second straight week he was fined. The officials, for whatever reason, don't often call penalties for illegal use of the helmet. That's what made the penalty called on Skattebo so unusual. The fact that the hit flattened Texans safety M.J. Stewart likely was a factor in the decision to penalize Skattebo. Still, the fact that only one of eight instances resulted in a foul being called underscores the fact that, when it comes to the rule against lowering the helmet and initiating forcible contact against an opponent, it's something that costs players money far more routinely than it costs their teams field position.

(Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero in ‘The Sweep,’ Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor is available via trade, but it would take a significant draft capital haul for the franchise to part with its last remaining key veteran pillar : Colts RB Jonathan Taylor: How expensive would it be to get Taylor out of Indianapolis? The Colts have already been offered a 2027 second-round draft pick plus an additional pick for Taylor—and they immediately rejected it. Even after trading Nelson and Buckner, the Colts aren’t in fire sale mode. Taylor is only 27, he is the face of the franchise, and he just signed a two-year, $44 million contract extension in August. The Colts won’t deal him for anything other than a premium haul—and rightfully so. The Colts haven’t told other teams exactly what they want for Taylor, but it makes sense they’d want something close to deal the Panthers got when they traded Christian McCaffrey to San Francisco in 2022 in exchange for 2023 second-, third-, and fourth-round picks plus a 2024 fifth-rounder. Taylor is due about $4.866 million for the rest of this season, including active roster bonuses. His $15 million base salary for 2027 becomes fully guaranteed five days after the Super Bowl. The Colts reportedly were quick to turn down overtures of a second round pick, as Indianapolis appears to be holding out hope for at least a first round pick to part with their star workhorse during a busy week for the franchise, which already saw the Horseshoe trade fellow veterans Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. It’s already been reported that Colts team owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon, who met with Taylor earlier this week, considers him potentially a major piece of the ongoing rebuild that was recently jumpstarted after such a disappointing start to Indianapolis’ season (at 2-5), that also saw longtime general manager Chris Ballard, the NFL executive who traded for and drafted Taylor back in the 2nd round of the 2020 NFL Draft, recently fired. Per ESPN’s Stephen Holder and longtime CBS 4/FOX 59’s Mike Chappell, while the Colts are currently listening on offers for Taylor from prospective trade suitors, Indianapolis isn’t actively shopping the franchise’s 2nd all-time career rushing leader (8,185) and all-time rushing touchdowns leader (77) either: One other point on Jonathan Taylor: There is a difference between shopping a player and taking calls. I would not describe what the Colts are doing as “shopping” JT. Might just be semantics but I thought it was worth mentioning. — Stephen Holder (@HolderStephen) October 31, 2026 JT and trade speculation. From everything I know and I’m out there all the time, of course the Colts are taking calls on JT availability/compensation. I don’t get the idea at all they are reaching out. They don’t need to and I believe Carlie wants JT to be part of rebuild. But if… — Mike Chappell (@mchappell51) October 31, 2026 On the season, Taylor has 140 carries for 587 total rushing yards (4.2 ypc. avg.) and 8 rushing touchdowns during all 7 starts. The expectation remains that if Taylor is still on the team, he’ll be active for Sunday’s game on the road against the Jacksonville Jaguars, per usual. Among suitors, there’s been reports that the Cincinnati Bengals, Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, and New England Patriots are among the teams that have already called and expressed interest in Taylor to the Colts regarding various degrees. However, again, the Colts have to be “blown away” by an offer, which likely means at least a first round pick to help Indianapolis get back into ‘Day 1,’ having also traded their 2027 first for Sauce Gardner in a premium package ahead of last year’s trade deadline. It’s a fair question though whether Indianapolis should seriously consider trading Taylor now to maximize the possible draft capital return, given that he is 27-years-old, has heavy mileage on his tires, and running backs don’t tend to age all that gracefully entering their thirties (unless you’re Derrick Henry and very few others). Meaning Taylor may only have 2-3 peak years left, which is realistically the amount of total time that it will take the Colts to fully complete a successful rebuild—that is, if all goes according to their next plan.

stories.title: Quenton Nelson arrives as Seahawks RBs cleared to return vs Bears
stories.summary: Fans have been waiting to see how Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price can spark the Seahawks running game. Now appears to be the time to learn.
stories.detailText: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - DECEMBER 26: Running back Zach Charbonnet #26 of the Seattle Seahawks carries the ball during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Chicago Bears, at Soldier Field on December 26, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images After thoroughly handling the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7, the Seattle Seahawks are set to host a second straight contender at Lumen Field on Monday Night Football in Week 8. The Chicago Bears come to town equipped with the newly acquired Jeffery Simmons, who instantly changes the capabilities of the Chicago defensive line, while the Seahawks will have at their disposal the services of six-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson. The addition of Nelson comes at an opportune time, as starting left tackle Charles Cross will miss the matchup against Chicago as he continues to work his way back from an ankle injury suffered against Kansas City, while former starting right guard Anthony Bradford is questionable with a knee issue. Cross’ absence and the addition of Nelson means Josh Jones will be at left tackle, with Grey Zabel sliding over to right guard. That will mark the first time those three start at those positions for the Seahawks this season, just as the ground game looks to get going with neither Zach Charbonnet nor Jadarian Price carrying a gameday designation. Of course, as John Boyle of the Seahawks points out, although Price does not have a designation heading into the game, the team would still need to move Price to the 53 man roster ahead of 4 pm New York time on Monday in order for him to suit up and play against the Bears. To clarify, Price has no status because he’s good, medically, but the Seahawks would still have to make a move by Monday to get him on the 53 if he’s going to play. — John Boyle (@johnpboyle) October 31, 2026 Seahawks have ruled out Charles Cross, Rashid Shaheed, Velus Jones Jr. No designation for Jadarian Price or Zach Charbonnet. Uchenna Nwosu doubtful. Anthony Bradford, Drew Lock, Patrick O’Connell, Brandon Pili questionable. — Curtis Crabtree (@Curtis_Crabtree) October 31, 2026 In addition to Cross missing the Monday night matchup, Rashid Shaheed and Velus Jones have both been ruled out, and Uchenna Nwosu is listed as doubtful, meaning it is unlikely he suits up. Also designated as questionable alongside Bradford are Drew Lock, Patrick O’Connell and Brandon Pili.

stories.title: Position grades from Michigan Football’s narrow win at Rutgers
stories.summary: It once again wasn’t pretty, but Michigan Football got back in the win column by defeating Rutgers, 28-21. Here are our position grades from the game:
stories.detailText: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 31: Salesi Moa #12 of the Michigan Wolverines celebrates a catch against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the first half at SHI Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images True to form, Michigan made things interesting, but still got the win 28-21 over Rutgers on Saturday. It definitely wasn’t perfect, but here’s a look at how each position group graded out in the victory. Quarterback – A- After a less-than-stellar debut as the starting quarterback last week, Tommy Carr looked really good against Rutgers. Granted, it was against a defense that isn’t scaring anyone (even on Halloween), but Carr went 22-of-27 for 266 yards and one touchdown. He also added 54 yards on the ground (82 excluding sacks) with two scores. The ground game was where Carr made his biggest impact, with his fourth-quarter touchdown deciding the game. He also extended several plays that he wasn’t well-protected and ended up being able to make something out of nothing through the air. He’ll get to make his first start in a rivalry game next week against Michigan State. ANOTHER TOMMY CARR RUSHING TOUCHDOWN! @UMichFootball pic.twitter.com/MKWqevvL19 — FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) October 31, 2026 Running Back – C Once again, the run game wasn’t impressive, with fault falling on both the offensive line and the running backs. Jordan Marshall wasn’t featured past the start of the game and had five carries for zero yards, despite scoring a two-yard touchdown. Savion Hiter was the featured back and had a decent performance with 20 carries for 76 yards. Bryson Kuzdzal was pretty efficient with 37 yards on just six carries. Had the run game been better, this one probably wouldn’t have been nearly as close. Wide Receiver – B With Carr looking more comfortable, the pass game got going a bit more than we’ve seen recently. Andrew Marsh was Michigan’s leading receiver with seven receptions for 51 yards while also getting interfered with on what would’ve been a deep touchdown pass in the fourth quarter. JJ Buchanan had another solid performance with five receptions for 63 yards, including an impressive touchdown grab on which he was interfered with and still made the play. Salesi Moa also continues to get involved and had a 44-yard catch-and-run on the opening drive of the game. Blocking on the perimeter was rough, but the receivers did their primary job of getting open a lot more. Tight End – B- Carr was able to spread the ball around a bit, leading to the tight ends being much more involved. Hogan Hansen reeled in three passes for 42 yards, continuing to be a nice safety valve in the short passing game. Mason Bonner also made his first reception of the season with a 27-yard grab in the first quarter. Meanwhile, Jalen Hoffman had two receptions for 17 yards. Continuing to get this group involved can be really helpful in making the offense more productive down the stretch, Offensive Line – D+ Michigan got right tackle Blake Frazier back in the starting lineup and rolled with Brady Norton and Nathan Efobi as the starting guards. Going up against one of the worst defensive fronts in the conference, Michigan’s offensive line still wasn’t able to put anything promising together, struggling in both the run and pass games. Of note, Norton did go down with an injury in the third quarter, while center Jake Guarnera, who’s been Michigan’s best offensive lineman all season, also came up hobbled in the fourth quarter. Both their statuses will be worth monitoring heading into next week. Defensive Line – C+ Michigan’s defense struggled on Saturday, giving up its highest point total of the season. The issues started up front with the defensive line, which failed to take advantage of a bad Rutgers offensive line. The pass rush was pretty quiet all day, but the run game was a bit more stout, holding Rutgers to 126 yards on the ground with just 54 of those coming on one run by Antwan Raymond. On the bright side, sophomore Benny Patterson broke out with the best day of any Wolverine defensive lineman, leading the team in tackles with seven. Linebacker – B- It’s not saying much, but the linebackers were the best defensive position group against Rutgers. They did a nice job keeping Rutgers’ run game in check (save for the Raymond run) and generating some modest pressure on quarterback A.J. Surace. The lone major blemish came in coverage when Nathaniel Staehling got burned in coverage by Raymond for a 32-yard gain in the second quarter. Overall though, there wasn’t nearly as much havoc as we’ve seen from the linebackers in previous games. Secondary – D Michigan’s secondary had a rough afternoon, making a handful of mistakes that played a role in making this a close game. Jyaire Hill, Smith Snowden and Zeke Berry were all tagged for penalties to help Rutgers get downfield, even with its backup quarterback throwing the ball up for grabs much of the time. There was also a blown coverage in the second quarter on which Snowden fell down, allowing Jourdin Houston to score on an 80-yard play. There were also dropped interceptions by Snowden and Mason Curtis. The secondary has been in the good graces of fans for much of the year, so hopefully this performance doesn’t become a trend. Special Teams – D+ The special teams continued to be pretty bad. Kicker Trey Butkowski once again missed two field goals, coming from 38 and 45 yards out. Additionally, the Wolverines were flagged on a confusing kick-catch interference that negated a muffed punt, which would’ve set Michigan’s offense up with an instant red zone opportunity. The blunders didn’t cost the Wolverines in this game, but things have been trending downward in the third phase of the game for a few weeks now. Rutgers tries to field the punt return, calls fair catch and gets a very lucky catch interference penalty. 👉 https://t.co/RjS0ydBMXi pic.twitter.com/PurDboEyxG — Richie O’Leary (@On3Richie) October 31, 2026 Coaching – D Michigan accomplished probably its two biggest goals of the week in getting the win and making its offense more functional. But the fact this game was close at all is still an indictment of those at the top of the program. Michigan pretty much sleepwalked through this game and showed to be pretty undisciplined once again with seven penalties for 90 yards, but avoided what would’ve been its worst loss to date. Next week, Michigan will get to take on a Michigan State team that will surely be ready to play. Let’s see how Kyle Whittingham can prepare his team for a rivalry game that will draw plenty of attention despite down years for both teams.

stories.title: Chargers place Derwin James on Injured Reserve after hamstring setback
stories.summary: Star safety Derwin James' setback is just the latest blow to an injury-riddled Chargers team as their season continues to spiral.
stories.detailText: Another brutal injury blow to the Los Angeles Chargers . Derwin James is headed to injured reserve, the team announced Saturday, Oct. 31. The news comes days after head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters that James had suffered a setback in his return from a hamstring injury that has kept the All-Pro safety sidelined since Week 3. This move pushes James' timeline back to a Week 12 return against the New England Patriots at the earliest. The Chargers will also be without guard Kayode Awosika (fibula), defensive back Deane Leonard (concussion) and receiver Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams . Corners Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley are questionable as of Friday's injury report. Ladd McConkey sat out Monday's practice with a concussion but was a full participant in practice the rest of the week and is expected to play. James' setback is the latest in a litany of injuries to key players that have come to mire the winless Chargers' season. Tight end David Njoku injured his right knee/fibula in Week 2. Left tackle Rashawn Slater underwent surgery after suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 4. Three additional offensive linemen are on the IR, with center Tyler Biadasz out for the season after tearing his ACL during a joint practice with the San Francisco 49ers in August. All in all, the Bolts now have nine players on the IR with the addition of James. The 30-year-old out of Florida State has 21 total tackles, 12 solo tackles and a pass defended in three games played this season. Elijah Molden, Tony Jefferson, and Genesis Smith have played well in James' absence, despite the team's record. They'll now be asked to hold the secondary down even longer. stories.title: Ravens defense has provided tough test for Josh Allen
stories.summary: Examining how Allen has played against the Ravens defense
stories.detailText: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has started against the Ravens six times — including the playoffs — in his NFL career before Week 8’s clash, and he hasn’t exactly flourished in those matchups with Baltimore. He’s been surprisingly held in check as a runner too. Allen’s average completion percentage in those six games is just 59.3%. His passing-yard average is just 211 with a pedestrian 6.06 yards-per-attempt average, and his rating is a mere 82.7. However, his touchdown-to-interception ratio is 5 to 1. His highest rushing-yard total (70) came in a 23-20 comeback in 2022. Other than that, Baltimore has held Allen to 30 yards or less on the ground. Allen has played the Ravens defense three times the past two years (twice in 2024), and of course, Baltimore’s personnel has changed over that time to a certain degree, but key pieces like Roquan Smith, Kyle Hamilton, and Marlon Humphrey remain. Despite his relative struggles against the Ravens in his NFL career to date… we can’t forget about Allen’s most recent outing facing this Baltimore team. Through three quarters in Week 1 last season, Allen was 18-of-26 for 143 yards with one touchdown through the air and no interceptions. Then he erupted. In the Bills’ furious comeback, Allen went 15-of-20 for 251 yards with one passing touchdown and two scores on the ground… in the fourth quarter of Buffalo’s 41-40 victory. He finished with 394 yards passing. Let’s see if that season-opening game a year ago was a turning point for Allen in his games against the Ravens defense.
