stories.summary: The Broncos suffer a big blow to their offense. According to reports, the Denver Broncos have placed second-year running back RJ Harvey on short-term injured reserve, sidelining him for at least the next four games. Harvey suffered a knee injury during practice this week and will now be eligible to come off the injure…
stories.detailText: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos runs during the first quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. The Broncos defeated the Cardinals 30-16. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Broncos suffer a big blow to their offense. According to reports, the Denver Broncos have placed second-year running back RJ Harvey on short-term injured reserve, sidelining him for at least the next four games. Harvey suffered a knee injury during practice this week and will now be eligible to come off the injured reserve for the Broncos’ home game vs. the Miami Dolphins on December 6th. To replace his spot on the Broncos’ 53-man roster, the team is reportedly signing veteran safety Taylor Rapp to the active roster, and he will start in place of the injured Talanoa Hufanga. The #Broncos are placing emerging RB R.J. Harvey on short-term IR as he recovers from the knee injury he suffered in practice this week, source says. Harvey will miss the next four games and is eligible to return as soon as the #Broncos game vs the #Dolphins on Dec. 6. pic.twitter.com/wBTJw6KHv4 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) October 31, 2026 Harvey, who had a 50+ yard touchdown this past Sunday vs. the Arizona Cardinals on a screen play, has been the Broncos’ most consistent offensive playmaker. Now, the Broncos will be down another running back as they head into the second half of their schedule. Rookie Jonah Coleman is expected to be the Broncos’ lead back this Sunday, with veteran JK Dobbins serving as the backup, and Cody Schrader being elevated from the practice squad to be the Broncos RB3. With Harvey and Tyler Badie on the short-term IR and JK Dobbins struggling, the Broncos could pursue another back on the trade market. As we talked about this morning, the Colts made star running back Jonathan Taylor available on the trade market, and the Broncos were among the teams listed as intereste d. Could the Harvey injury make them go all-in and acquire Taylor? Other backs like Saquon Barkley, Tony Pollard, and maybe even Breece Hall are rumored to be backs on the trade block as we come closer to the NFL trade deadline, so we will have to see if the Broncos make a move. Right now, they have a currently unproven and inexperienced (Just 19 carries on the season) rookie back in Jonah Coleman and a struggling veteran JK Dobbins, as their rushers. They are just one injury away from Cody Schrader, a practice squad player, seeing significant snaps on offense. I believe they need to add some more depth to their running back room moving forward as we head into the colder months of the season. At the end of the day, this is a major blow to the Broncos’ offense. Harvey has been one of their more consistent and explosive playmakers this season, and now he will be sidelined for at least the next 5 weeks (4 games + bye week). We will have to see if this injury forces the Broncos into making a move for another running back in the coming days.

stories.title: Seahawks star Uchenna Nwosu fined for horse-collar tackle on Patrick Mahomes
stories.summary: Two more of these infractions would put Nwosu in automatic one-game suspension territory.
stories.detailText: The Seattle Seahawks played their most complete game of the season last Sunday, routing the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 behind efficient offense and a masterful defensive performance. They did not, however, come away unscathed in the NFL’s fine book. Unsurprisingly, edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu was docked some money after he was penalized for a horse-collar tackle on Patrick Mahomes. Nwosu was held on the same play, so there were offsetting penalties called and a replayed down. On the next snap, Derick Hall had a crunching strip-sack on the Chiefs quarterback, but neither Nwosu nor Jarran Reed could recover the loose ball, and Mahomes somehow recovered his own fumble to preserve Kansas City’s eventual field goal. Rumor has it that Mike Tirico is still saying, “STILL OUT!” to this day. Seahawks edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu was fined $17,911 for his horse-collar tackle of Patrick Mahomes. It was the only fine on either team. pic.twitter.com/fWWiJaTxVg — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) October 31, 2026 Horse-collar tackles are among the offenses that the NFL has deemed suspension worthy for repeat offenders. If Nwosu commits two more horse-collar penalties this year, he will serve an automatic one-game ban. No other Seahawks were fined. The immediate greater worry for Nwosu is his availability for Monday night against the Chicago Bears, as he’s listed as doubtful for the game.

stories.title: Patriots add running back Lan Larison to 53, elevate former Dolphins wideout from practice squad
stories.summary: Sunday’s AFC East kickoff in Miami Gardens is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.
stories.detailText: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: Lan Larison #34 of the New England Patriots looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After downgrading running back TreVeyon Henderson and wide receiver A.J. Brown to out, the New England Patriots traveled to Hard Rock Stadium with insurance at both positions. The organization promoted running back Lan Larison to the 53-man roster and elevated wide receiver Ryan Miller from the practice squad for Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins. Larison, 24, will serve as the third option in the running back room behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner after an illness thinned the depth chart. The 5-foot-11, 209-pound change of pace reverted to the practice squad in September after making his NFL debut versus the Seattle Seahawks. He caught two passes for nine yards and averaged 24.5 yards per kickoff return in the Super Bowl LX rematch, handling three snaps on offense and six snaps on special teams. Arriving in Foxborough as an undrafted free agent in 2025, Larison spent his rookie campaign on injured reserve following a foot injury. The UC Davis product cleared waivers at the 53-man deadline in August and was retained on the 17-man scout team at its formation. Two months later, he takes the open spot on the active roster. Miller, 26, signed to the Patriots’ practice squad midway through October after Romeo Doubs joined fellow veteran target Mack Hollins on injured reserve. The 6-foot-2, 217-pound standard call-up will head back to his former stomping grounds as the fourth healthy wide receiver behind DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. Currently ranking fifth on the Dolphins in receiving yards, Miller reeled in a season-long, 77-yard touchdown from quarterback Malik Willis before making his way to Gillette Stadium. Originally entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie in 2023, the Furman alum spent three years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before being claimed off waivers by the New York Giants and then by Miami during training camp. He has appeared in 30 NFL games, including six starts, while totaling 17 receptions for 254 yards and four touchdowns. Linebacker Christian Elliss and cornerback Carlton Davis III move forward with questionable game statuses for the Patriots following the downgrades, while offensive tackle Marcus Bryant will remain on injured reserve for the divisional matchup. Sunday’s kickoff in Miami Gardens is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

stories.title: 'No way' that Jets trade star WR Garrett Wilson before deadline, source says
stories.summary: The Jets are not expected to trade Garrett Wilson, sources told ESPN, despite increased speculation about the star wide receiver's future.
stories.detailText: As trade talks ramp up across the NFL, there is one player who isn't going anywhere before the deadline despite increased speculation: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson . One well-placed source told ESPN this weekend that there is "no way" the Jets will trade Wilson by the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline, despite any interest from other teams. The Jets might have said the same thing a year ago in regard to cornerback Sauce Gardner and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams , only to trade both on deadline day for a bevy of draft picks. But sources said the situation this year with Wilson is different for various reasons. The Tennessee Titans told teams there was no way they would trade perennial Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons -- until they did Thursday, when they received two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick from the Chicago Bears . But Wilson does seem untouchable before the deadline. For starters, the Jets have no interest in moving on from Wilson, 26, who is considered to be one of the most talented wide receivers in the NFL. The Jets signed him to a four-year, $130 million extension that runs through 2030 a mere 15 months ago. Additionally, Jets ownership is said to love Wilson and would want no part of trading him, according to sources. The Jets already have amassed a surplus of draft picks -- the Indianapolis Colts ' 2027 first-round pick and the higher of Dallas ' or Green Bay 's 2027 first-round pick -- in exchange for Gardner and Williams. At some point, New York needs to prioritize making picks, not accumulating them. That is the exact plan with Wilson, who is viewed as a central building block as the Jets look to replenish their roster and get stronger on offense in the 2027 draft. Wilson recently told reporters that he did not want to be traded. "I want to be here, man," he said. "I want to win games, and that's the one thing we've been missing on here. I love it here. Do I love it more than I love winning? Nah, to be completely honest, but I'm hopeful. "I've never been the best optimistic guy, but I've found a way and dug deep, and I've been optimistic for three, four, five years now. And that's why these [losses] each weekend hurt a little more." Other wide receiver names continue to come up in connection to the trade deadline: Jacksonville 's Brian Thomas Jr. , Indianapolis' Josh Downs , Minnesota 's Jauan Jennings , Cleveland 's Jerry Jeudy , Tennessee's Calvin Ridley and even Wilson. The other receivers might be attainable in the days leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, but Wilson is not.

stories.title: Bills add defensive backs from practice squad for tomorrow’s game vs. Ravens
stories.summary: The Bills have added some more secondary help before Week 8’s game vs. Ravens
stories.detailText: The Buffalo Bills have been reeling in the secondary, and signs are pointing to more reinforcements in said secondary for the enormous showdown with Lamar Jackson and the Ravens tomorrow. At 4:00pm on Saturday, the team announced moves that will make a trio of practice-squad defensive backs available for this Week 8 contest inside the new Highmark Stadium: Roster moves: – Signed DB Te’Cory Couch from the practice squad. – Elevated S Geno Stone and CB A.J. Woods from the practice squad. — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) October 31, 2026 Couch being signed from the practice squad is different from being elevated — players are only allowed to be elevated three times during the regular season, so this transaction will not be counted for Couch on that front. stories.title: T'Vondre Sweat placed on injured reserve with knee injury
stories.summary: The Jets will be without T'Vondre Sweat for at least the next four games, as the starting nose tackle was placed on injured reserve Saturday with a knee sprain.
stories.detailText: FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets will be without T'Vondre Sweat for at least the next four games, as the starting nose tackle was placed on injured reserve Saturday with a knee sprain. The good news for Sweat is that it's not considered a season-ending injury, a source said. The 366-pound run stuffer will be eligible to return Nov. 29 against the Miami Dolphins . Sweat already had been ruled out for Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) at MetLife Stadium. His injury, which occurred last Sunday, comes at an inopportune time for the Jets, who have been struggling to stop the run. They're allowing 127.7 yards per game, 24th in the NFL. Rookie Darrell Jackson Jr. , a fourth-round pick from Florida State, is expected to replace Sweat in the lineup. The Jets (2-5), losers of two straight, don't expect to have rookie edge rusher David Bailey (groin), who is doubtful for the game. To replace Sweat and Bailey on the game-day roster, they brought up Payton Page (signed to the roster) and Quinton Bell (elevation) from the practice squad, respectively. The Jets are thin at defensive tackle. They're already down David Onyemata (core muscle surgery), who was placed on IR in Week 3. Sweat was acquired in an offseason trade with the Tennessee Titans . After missing a chunk of training camp with a hamstring injury, he has appeared in all seven games, with no sacks, two tackles-for-loss and 17 total tackles.

stories.title: Cleveland Browns roster moves: Things going Cleveland’s way, finally
stories.summary: Cleveland’s offensive line will be intact for Sunday’s divisional showdown with Pittsburgh.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Al Pereira/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns received a bit of good news on Saturday regarding the game-day roster for Sunday’s key divisional game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Starting right tackle Tytus Howard, who was originally listed as questionable while dealing with a concussion, cleared the league-mandated concussion protocol on Saturday and can play on Sunday. That means the Browns will be at full strength on the offensive line as they look to break a 23-year, regular-season losing streak to the Steelers in Pittsburgh. Starting cornerback Myles Harden is still questionable, however, as he is dealing with a hamstring injury, which could test Cleveland’s depth in the secondary if Harden is not able to go. The Browns appear to be confident, however, as they only made one practice squad elevation for the game, and that was to elevate rookie tight end Carsen Ryan from the practice squad. Ryan was released prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans to open a roster spot for running back Dylan Sampson to return from injured reserve, and subsequently signed back with the Browns to their practice squad. The seventh-round selection from BYU has played in six games for the Browns, but has only played two snaps on offense, registering no stats, and 73 snaps on special teams, making one tackle. Pittsburgh made a pair of roster moves on Saturday, signing wide receiver Brandon Smith to the 53-man roster from the practice squad, and elevating wide receiver Brandon Johnson from the practice squad. stories.title: Eagles roster news: 2 moves announced ahead of Commanders game
stories.summary: Week 8 updates.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Elijah Mitchell #49 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced two roster moves ahead of the team’s Week 8 Sunday night game against the Washington Commanders. Here’s an overview: RB Elijah Mitchell and EDGE Mason Reiger were temporarily elevated from the practice squad. Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. ELIJAH MITCHELL Saquon Barkley will play against the Commanders despite being listed under “did not participate” on Wednesday and Thursday before being upgraded to limited on Friday. It remains to be seen how much of a workload he can handle; Barkley was clearly playing through discomfort from his hamstring and back injuries in Week 7. He was ultimately limited to 10 snaps on Monday night. Jaydon Blue, who was promoted from the practice squad earlier this week, is the only other Eagles running back on the roster. The Eagles previously had him active for Week 6 but did not play him at all despite injuries knocking them down to Dameon Pierce (who is now on injured reserve) as the only backfield option in that game. By elevating Mitchell, the Eagles now have three running backs for Sunday’s game. He could also factor in as a kick returner with Britan Covey out. This is Mitchell’s second temporary elevation this season. He only has one more remaining. MASON REIGER Reiger is set to make his Eagles debut after originally joining Philadelphia’s practice squad on August 31. The Eagles are currently banged up at edge rusher, sort of. It’s not to the point where their edge rushers won’t suit up for Sunday’s game. But it is to the point where Jalyx Hunt and Jonathan Greenard saw way fewer snaps than normal in Week 7. Nolan Smith is also coming off a concussion while Arnold Ebiketie has been playing a lot due to the other injuries at his position. Reiger likely won’t play much, if at all, on defense but he’s around for depth purposes in addition to contributing on special teams. NON-MOVES For the third game in a row, Zach Ertz will sit out while being on the practice squad. The Eagles already used up his three temporary elevations, so, he can only play if he’s on the roster. And the Eagles have instead opted to go with Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, Eli Stowers, and Grant Calcaterra as their top four tight ends. Maybe the plan is to bring Ertz up if/when the Eagles deal Goedert ahead of the NFL trade deadline? We’ll see. In the meantime, Ertz continues to be seven receptions away from tying the Eagles’ all-time franchise record in that category. The Eagles notably did NOT activate Jakorian Bennett from injured reserve, despite the fact that top backup cornerback Jonathan Jones has been ruled out of Sunday’s game. With the Eagles opening Bennett’s 21-day practice window to return from IR on October 14, the time to activate him is running out. In the meantime, Kelee Ringo and/or Mac McWilliams could see snaps on defense if the Eagles’ corner depth is tested. Interesting to see that the Eagles went with temporarily elevating Reiger instead of 2026 rookie Keyshawn James-Newby. KJN previously got the nod the last two weeks and has one elevation remaining. The Eagles are entering Sunday’s game with just three healthy off-ball linebackers: Zack Baun, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. (starting in place of an injured Jihaad Campbell), and Smael Mondon. The team did not opt to temporarily elevate Anfernee Orji from the practice squad to have a fourth player at this position.

stories.title: Source: Commanders DT Daron Payne suffered season-ending foot injury
stories.summary: Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture in practice Friday, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
stories.detailText: ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne suffered a season-ending Jones fracture in practice Friday, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter. The injury occurred late in a light practice, during a team drill, according to a team source. It was described as a fluke injury, not resulting from anyone stepping on his foot during a play. Payne will be placed on injured reserve and calls his future in Washington into question. He's in the final year of his contract and turns 30 in May. A typical recovery for such an injury could take up to four months, according to medical experts. Payne is the Commanders' longest-tenured position player. It's a tough blow for Washington (1-4-1) which plays the Eagles (2-5) Sunday night. The Commanders will already be without starting end Javon Kinlaw , out Sunday with a knee injury. They do have depth at the position with veterans Charles Omenihu and Deatrich Wise Jr . DL Jer'Zhan Newton , a second-round pick in 2024, returned to practice this week after suffering a torn pectoral muscle during a preseason game on Aug. 14, but he was ruled out Saturday. Payne has been a longtime starter for Washington. In fact, he started every game between 2020 and '24 as well as the first six games this season. He missed only two games in 2025. Payne made the Pro Bowl in 2022 when he recorded a career-best 11 sacks -- six more than his second best season. He had one sack this year but was averaging a career-best 2.8 pass rush wins per game according to Tru Media. Washington drafted Payne in the first round of the 2018 draft and signed him to a four-year extension in March of 2023.

stories.title: Patriots rule out A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson vs. Dolphins
stories.summary: Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. In addition, No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson has been ruled out due to an illness.
stories.detailText: FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown has been ruled out for Sunday's road game against the Miami Dolphins , the team announced Saturday. Brown had a knee issue flare up this week, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. In addition, No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson has been ruled out due to an illness, according to the team. Henderson missed practice on Thursday and Friday. The Patriots had one open spot on their 53-man roster and signed first-year running back Lan Larison from their practice squad to fill it on Saturday. The team also elevated fourth-year receiver Ryan Miller from the practice squad for the game. As for Brown, he was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and later that day, his designation on the injury report had changed. It noted the knee issue, in addition to the right high ankle sprain sustained in the season opener that had landed him on injured reserve. "Just wasn't able to finish practice on Wednesday, so we continue to treat him," coach Mike Vrabel said Friday. Prior to that practice, Brown acknowledged he was still managing the ankle injury and didn't have his trademark explosiveness on an every-play basis. But Brown made it clear he wasn't making excuses, adding, "None of that stuff matters. I'm out here, so I'm going." The Patriots had Brown going as if he had never been sidelined due to the ankle injury sustained in the season opener. In his first action since being designated to return from IR on Oct. 14, Brown played 102 out of a possible 122 snaps in a win over the New York Jets on Oct. 18 and a loss to the Chicago Bears on Oct. 22. He admitted the stretch of two games in five days was "a lot for anyone" and appreciated "the couple [extra] days [off] on the back end." He had expressed hope Wednesday he would have a full week of practice and "try to put my best foot forward on Sunday [in Miami]." Then came the knee flare-up, which leaves the Patriots thin at receiver with DeMario "Pop" Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III the only healthy receivers on the 53-man roster. Vrabel said the team's approach with Brown in the two games, and the injury that led him to miss Sunday's game, are "separate issues here." Asked about the heavy workload for Brown, and if he would have benefited from fewer snaps, Vrabel said: "We want our best players to play and we consider him one of those." Meanwhile, with Henderson out, the Patriots now have Rhamondre Stevenson , Corey Kiner and Larison as running backs on the 53-man roster.

stories.title: Michigan Football defeats Rutgers behind QB Tommy Carr’s go-ahead TD
stories.summary: Michigan Football defeated Rutgers, 28-21, behind QB Tommy Carr’s go-ahead TD in the final minutes. Here’s the recap, highlights and stats:
stories.detailText: Oct 31, 2026; Piscataway, New Jersey, USA; Michigan Wolverines quarterback Tommy Carr (14) scrambles during the first half as Rutgers Scarlet Knights defensive lineman Rondo Porter (99) defends at SHI Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Michigan Wolverines got back in the win column with a 28-21 win over the Rutgers Scarlet Knights on Saturday. Michigan improved to 5-3 overall and 2-3 in Big Ten play, as quarterback Tommy Carr erupted for a career-high 320 total yards and a go-ahead touchdown in the final minutes of the game. Here’s the recap, highlights and stats. First quarter Michigan put together a 10-play, 92-yard drive to open the game, as Carr connected with wide receiver JJ Buchanan for a six-yard touchdown reception to take a 7-0 lead. Just moments before, Carr found wide receiver Salesi Moa for a 44-yard gain. JJ went up and got it! 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/5EpoGeSN5Y — Michigan Football (@UMichFootball) October 31, 2026 It was an impressive possession for Michigan, scoring an opening drive touchdown for just the second time this season. Carr connected on 4-for-5 passing attempts, including finding wide receiver Andrew Marsh for consecutive first downs. Rutgers was hoping to respond with a touchdown of its own, but the drive eventually stalled as Michigan cornerback Smith Snowden had a clutch tackle to force a field goal. The Scarlet Knights cut the deficit to 7-3 with a 46-yard field goal. Second quarter The Wolverines continued to play at a high level offensively, scoring another touchdown to extend the lead to 14-3. Carr hit Buchanan for 30 yards to get into the red zone, and running back Jordan Marshall scored on a two-yard touchdown run. Jordan Marshall finds a hole to extend the @UMichFootball lead 💪 Watch on @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/xyws2AWsj6 — Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) October 31, 2026 It appeared Michigan was going to get a quick stop and force a punt, as edge rusher Benny Patterson III had a sack and tackle for loss. However, Snowden fell down and allowed Rutgers to score an 80-yard touchdown pass to trim it to 14-10. SURACE FINDS HOUSTON FOR THE 80-YD @RFootball TD 😱 Watch on BTN pic.twitter.com/oXKz3P48kL — Big Ten Network (@BigTenNetwork) October 31, 2026 Michigan had a chance to extend the lead, but kicker Trey Butkowski continued to struggle for a second straight week, missing a 48-yard field goal. Following a successful field goal from Rutgers, the Wolverines took a 14-13 lead into halftime. HALFTIME: Michigan 14, Rutgers 13 Third quarter The Wolverines started the second half just like the first half, marching down the field with an 11-play, 75-yard drive. Buchanan and Marsh had first-down receptions, and Carr scored on a 15-yard touchdown run to take a 21-13 lead. Tommy with the wheels! 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/5We94JDY51 — Michigan Football (@UMichFootball) October 31, 2026 On the ensuing drive, Michigan’s defense didn’t allow Rutgers to get any momentum as defensive tackle Enow Etta deflected a first down pass. Then, linebacker Troy Bowles recorded a tackle on back-to-back snaps to help force a punt. The Wolverines looked like they would extend the lead to double figures after runs from running backs Savion Hiter and Bryson Kuzdzal that led to first downs. However, Butkowski missed yet another field goal, so the lead remained at 21-13. Fourth quarter Early in the fourth quarter, Michigan seemingly recovered a muffed punt that would have set the Wolverines up with great field position. But a controversial kick-catch interference was called, so Rutgers kept possession. Rutgers took advantage of the new life, as running back Antwan Raymond took off for 54 yards to get in the red zone. Just moments later, Rutgers scored a touchdown and converted the two-point conversion to tie it up at 21-21 with 11:43 remaining. Two-point conversion is good ‼️ @RFootball ties this game up 👀 Watch on @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/uJwiMMTZp7 — Big Ten Football (@B1Gfootball) October 31, 2026 On the ensuing possession, Carr put the Wolverines on his back with a go-ahead 11-play, 75-yard drive to go up 28-21. Carr converted a pair of third downs by finding tight end Hogan Hansen and Buchanan to move the sticks. Following a first down run by Hiter, Carr escaped the pocket and weaved into the end zone for a nine-yard touchdown run. It was a great drive by the freshman, remaining poised and putting Michigan up with 4:24 to go in the game. Tommy Carr scrambles across the goal line to put @UMichFootball in front 🙌 Watch on BTN pic.twitter.com/aVpJN4N5xT — Big Ten Network (@BigTenNetwork) October 31, 2026 The Wolverines got a defensive stop, as safety Mason Curtis recorded a pass break up and a tackle to help force a punt. With an opportunity to run out the rest of the clock, Carr pushed the pile for a game-sealing first down to secure a victory. FINAL: Michigan 28, Rutgers 21 Hail to the Victors! 〽️ pic.twitter.com/cxnwNpkaoF — Michigan Football (@UMichFootball) October 31, 2026 Michigan stat leaders QB Tommy Carr: 22-for-27, 266 passing yards, 1 passing touchdown, 54 rushing yards, 2 rushing touchdowns RB Savion Hiter: 20 carries, 76 rushing yards WR JJ Buchanan: 5 receptions, 63 receiving yards, 1 touchdown WR Andrew Marsh: 7 receptions, 51 receiving yards TE Hogan Hansen: 3 receptions, 42 receiving yards DE Benny Patterson III: 7 total tackles, 1 sack, 1 tackle for loss DB Chris Bracy: 6 total tackles, 1 sack, 1 tackle for loss DT Enow Etta: 2 total tackles, 1 sack, 1 tackle for loss, 1 pass deflection Rutgers stat leaders QB AJ Surace: 3-for-12, 123 passing yards, 1 touchdown RB Antwan Raymond: 11 carries, 85 rushing yards WR Jourdin Houston: 1 reception, 80 receiving yards, 1 touchdown DB JJ Conyers: 9 total tackles Up next Michigan will host the Michigan State Spartans next Saturday, Nov. 7, with a chance to secure a fifth straight win in the rivalry.

stories.title: NFL Week 8 Injury Report: A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson ruled out for Week 8, DJ Moore, Kincaid questionable
stories.summary: Track the injuries to know around the NFL, all in one place.
stories.detailText: Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in. Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. **UPDATED AS OF SATURDAY, OCTOBER 31 AT 4 PM ET** AFC East ◆ Buffalo Bills DJ Moore - WR (shoulder) Moore aggravated his shoulder injury in Week 4 and was forced from the game, unable to return. He did not play in Weeks 5-6. He was limited to begin Week 8, post-bye , and was listed questionable against the Ravens. Impact: The team's Week 7 bye should afford Moore the requisite time to heal and return to the active roster when the Bills take on the Ravens on the road. Moore would be an upside WR3 if active. Dalton Kincaid - TE (chest) Kincaid was limited on Wednesday before drawing the questionable tag for Week 8 against the Ravens. Impact: Kincaid exits the Bills' Week 7 bye with a chest injury. The development is unfortunate, but he is on track to play and can be treated as a TE1. ◆ Miami Dolphins De’Von Achane - RB (knee) Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season. Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright . The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season. Jaylen Wright - RB (foot/quad) Wright was unable to finish the team's Week 6 win over the Jets due to a hamstring injury. He is practicing fully in Week 8 . Impact: Wright barely qualifies as a bench stash. Malik Willis - QB (groin) Willis is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Patriots. Impact: Likely none, but it could impact his willingness to run. He remains a QB2. Malik Washington - WR (knee) Washington was limited on Wednesday but removed from the injury report Friday. he will play against the Patriots. Impact: Washington is on track to play, but he is only a WR5. Greg Dulcich ( ankle ) was limited as well, but he does not need to be rostered despite a productive Week 7. ◆ New England Patriots Mack Hollins - WR (calf) Hollins departed the team's Week 4 win over the Bills with a calf injury and did not return. He was placed on injured reserve in Week 5. Impact: Veteran practice squad call-up Efton Chism saw the biggest increase in routes following Hollins' departure, which was particularly interesting considering the team's general lack of downfield abilities. Perhaps Kyle Williams could finally see additional time on the field. Romeo Doubs - WR (shoulder) Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined. A.J. Brown - WR (ankle) Brown was limited on Wednesday but downgraded to "DNP" Thursday and Friday, ultimately ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins. Impact: Brown's absence leaves only DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism as healthy wide receivers currently on the roster. The most intriguing upside case to be made is with Williams in a potential full-time role on the perimeter, where his downfield acumen brings tantalizing ceiling. TreVeyon Henderson - RB (illness) Henderson was ruled out Saturday with an illness after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday. Impact: Rhamondre Stevenson should operate as a clear workhorse against the sieve-like Dolphins defense, while Corey Kiner is in line to serve as the primary change of pace option. Expect the team to elevate a running back from the practice squad later Saturday. Fantasy managers can start Stevenson as a clear RB2 with RB1 upside in the plus spot. ◆ New York Jets Breece Hall - RB (quadriceps) Hall is listed as questionable for Week 8 following a week of limited sessions. Impact: Hall would appear to be on track to resume lead-back duties for the Jets. Braelon Allen may have earned himself a weekly rushing role during Hall's absence, though we will not know for sure until this week's game transpires. Hall is a high-end RB2. Allen is flex-viable. AFC North ◆ Baltimore Ravens Lamar Jackson - QB (ankle) Jackson has been out since injuring his ankle in Week 4. He is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Bills and was confirmed as the starter by head coach Jesse Minter Friday . Impact: Jackson's return to face the Bills is a significant fantasy boon to Zay Flowers , who has been among the league's most efficient receivers this season. Adam Randall - RB (undisclosed) The Ravens activated Randall's 21-day practice window on Wednesday . Impact: Randall can be stashed in deep leagues. Durham Smythe - TE (Achilles) Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done. Impact: It was Matt Hibner who saw the largest increase in snaps following Smythe's departure in Week 4, making it unlikely we see veteran Mark Andrews in a more robust role. ◆ Cincinnati Bengals Ja’Marr Chase - (NIR-rest/ankle) Chase did not practice on Wednesday but was removed from the injury report Friday . Impact: This could be a non-issue, but NFL teams have played games with injury reports this year. Chase should be good to go for WR1 duties. Andrei Iosivas - WR (thumb) The Bengals placed Iosivas on injured reserve in Week 3 Impact: Wide receivers Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will duke it out for the No. 3 wide receiver role for at least the next four weeks. Meyers can be added in 14-team leagues, though his upside is questionable. Erick All - TE (knee) All suffered a torn ACL in Week 7. He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday and will miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: All loses yet another season in devastating fashion after suffering his third torn ACL. His absence could provide a slight uptick in snap rate and route participation for Mike Gesicki , although he will be a difficult weekly start for as long as both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain healthy. ◆ Cleveland Browns Dylan Sampson - RB (knee) Sampson was limited on Wednesday but removed from the injury report Friday . Impact: None. He is FLEX-viable. Raheim Sanders - RB (hip) The Browns placed Sanders on injured reserve in Week 6 . Impact: He will be eligible to return after four games missed. ◆ Pittsburgh Steelers Michael Pittman - WR (foot) Pittman was limited on Wednesday before being seen using a scooter in the locker room after practice . It was then revealed that Pittman aggravated his foot injury. The Steelers placed him on injured reserve late in Week 5 . Impact: Pittman's absence opens the door for additional opportunities behind DK Metcalf , a role that now appears to be on rookie Germie Bernard 's shoulders following the multi-week injury suffered by Roman Wilson in Week 5. Ben Skowronek ( calf ) resumed practicing in Week 8. Roman Wilson - WR (finger) Wilson departed in the second half of Week 5 with a finger injury and is reportedly looking at a multi-game absence. He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: See above. AFC South ◆ Houston Texans Jaylin Noel - WR (toe) Noel suffered a turf toe injury in Week 7. The Texans placed him on injured reserve in Week 8. He is expected to miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: Tank Dell and recent acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. would be in line to benefit. Harrison should be added in 12-team formats. David Montgomery - RB (groin) Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Montgomery is " week-to-week " with a groin injury. He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday, and remains sidelined to begin Week 7 . The team ruled him o ut for Week 7 on Friday. Impact: The expected multi-game absence leaves Woody Marks atop the backfield depth chart. He is a viable FLEX starter, but the Texans showed in Week 6 that they will continue splitting backfield touches. Jawhar Jordan - RB (undisclosed) The Texans placed Jordan on injured reserve in Week 7 . Impact: Jordan prevented Marks from handling a full-time role in Week 6. Dare Ogunbowale will probably do the same while Montgomery is sidelined. Jayden Higgins - WR (knee) Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp. Impact: It's a massive blow to a Texans team that was counting on Higgins taking another step forward in his Sophomore campaign. The team traded for Kayshon Boutte in the wake of the injury and then added Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Cardinals ahead of Week 6. ◆ Indianapolis Colts Alec Pierce - WR (heel) Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Head coach Shane Steichen said Pierce won’t practice this week. Impact: Josh Downs should serve as the primary option through the air for as long as Pierce remains sidelined. The team signed veteran field-stretcher Darius Slayton in the wake of Pierce's injury, although he is unlikely to return weekly fantasy production. Slayton (knee) was ruled out for Week 5 on Friday. Tyler Warren - TE (groin) Warren was added to the team's injury report on Friday and was designated questionable for Week 6. He did not play Week 7. After returning to practice Thursday, Warren will play in Week 8 against the Jaguars. Impact: Warren will warrant TE1 treatment upon returning. ◆ Jacksonville Jaguars Jakobi Meyers - WR (hamstring) Meyers was limited to begin Week 8 and downgraded to a 'DNP' Friday, ultimately listed as questionable for Week 8 against the Colts. Impact: Hamstring strains can be finicky at the wide receiver position, and we do not know when he suffered the injury. The Jaguars were on bye in Week 7. If active, Meyers warrants FLEX treatment, though the injured tissue would be prone to aggravation. ◆ Tennessee Titans Tyjae Spears - RB (knee) Spears is listed as questionable in what seems like a weekly occurrence. He ultimately did not play in Week 7. Spears remains sidelined to begin Week 8 and was ruled out Friday. Impact: Tony Pollard operated in a workhorse role in the absence of Spears in the team's Week 7 loss to the Browns, a setup that could persist should Spears miss additional time. Pollard is a middling RB2 without Spears in a difficult matchup. Carnell Tate - WR (shoulder) Tate did not practice throughout the week before being ruled out Friday. Impact: Wan'Dale Robinson is in line to serve as the top option through the air against the inside-funnel Cincinnati defense. He garners viable FLEX status. Calvin Ridley - WR (hip) Ridley was limited on Wednesday before drawing the questionable tag for Week 8. Impact: Ridley largely serves as an impediment to the Titans' young wide receivers. AFC West ◆ Denver Broncos Pat Bryant - WR (ankle) Bryant suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 4 loss to the 49ers and is reportedly expected to miss "a few weeks." He was placed on injured reserve on Friday. Impact: Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims appear to be the next men up in Bryant's absence, although the team could use a "sum of all parts" mentality to bridge his absence, considering historical trends. Alpha wide receiver Jaylen Waddle would be the primary beneficiary. Jaylen Waddle - WR (chest) Waddle was injured in the fourth quarter of the team's Week 7 win over the Cardinals and did not return. He was sidelined for Week 8's first practice before drawing the questionable tag for Week 8. Impact: Fantasy managers will want to track his status throughout the coming week ahead of a divisional tilt against the Chiefs. Waddle is too talented to sit on fantasy benches if active, regardless of the poor returns through the first seven weeks. RJ Harvey - RB (knee) Harvey popped on the injury report Thursday with a knee injury and was ruled out for Week 8 Friday. Impact: Harvey's absence returns the backfield to a two-way timeshare in the absence of Tyler Badie, with rookie Jonah Coleman the favorite for featured usage. Coleman can be started as a viable FLEX option in a difficult matchup against the Chiefs. ◆ Kansas City Chiefs Rashee Rice - WR (hamstring) Rice departed Week 4 with a hamstring injury. He resumed practicing in a limited capacity early in Week 8 and was removed from the injury report Friday . Impact: Wide receivers Jalen Royals , Andrew Armstrong and Cyrus Allen have received increased playing time, but none of the three are meaningfully separating. If Rice returns, he warrants WR3 treatment, at worst. Tyquan Thornton - WR (ankle) Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks. Impact: See above. ◆ Las Vegas Raiders Brock Bowers - TE (calf) Bowers was limited on Wednesday and removed from the injury report Friday. Impact: None. He's the overall TE1. Jack Bech - WR (forearm) The Raiders placed Bech on injured reserve in Week 4. He saw his 21-day practice window activated Tuesday and was activated from injured reserve Saturday. Impact : Bech returns as the third option through the air for an offense highly concentrated amongst Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker. He is worthy of a stash in deeper leagues. ◆ Los Angeles Chargers Ladd McConkey - WR (concussion) McConkey was forced from the team's Week 6 loss to the Chiefs due to a concussion after just eight offensive snaps. McConkey is practicing in full for Week 8 against the Rams, coming off the Chargers' Week 7 bye. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Rams. Impact: None. This is the Chargers' prove-it week. McConkey should be in starting lineups. Tre’ Harris - WR (hamstring) Harris missed the team's Week 6 loss to the Chiefs with a hamstring injury. He was limited to begin Week 8 but removed from the injury report Friday . Impact: Harris is a boom-bust FLEX in a difficult matchup against the Rams. David Njoku - TE (fibula) Njoku is looking at an extended absence after being carted from the field in the team's Week 2 loss to the Raiders. The Chargers placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . Impact: See above. NFC East ◆ Dallas Cowboys George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) Pickens has been playing through the shoulder injury for a while. The hamstring injury is new. Impact: If Picks injured his hamstring on Wednesday, he would likely miss this week's game, elevating Ryan Flournoy to the WR3/FLEX tier. Impact: The Cowboys released both Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah at roster cuts and now have only Emari Demercado on the active roster behind starter Javonte Williams . Expect Israel Abanikanda to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 2, while Williams appears likely to see all the work he can handle against the Commanders. Williams is a locked-in RB1. ◆ New York Giants Jaxson Dart - QB (knee) Dart injured his MCL, PCL and meniscus on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football against the Rams. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is possible for Dart to return in the postseason, although this is unlikely. Impact: Backup Jameis Winston was benched in favor of recent acquisition J.J. McCarthy in the second half of their loss to the Saints. Head coach John Harbaugh confirmed McCarthy as the starter for Week 7. The Athetic's Dan Duggan reported Tuesday that Likely should be fine after the team's Week 8 bye. Impact: Likely none. ◆ Philadelphia Eagles Saquon Barkley - RB (back/hamstring) Barkley returned from a two-game absence in Week 7, only to suffer an unrelated injury (back) in the second quarter. Barkley did not practice the following Wednesday, but reportedly expects to play this week . He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Commanders. Impact: Barkley is difficult to trust in a poor matchup considering his current ailments. Dameon Pierce - RB (undisclosed) Pierce was injured on a kick return in the fourth quarter of the team's Week 7 loss to the Cowboys. He was placed on injured reserve the following Wednesday . Impact: See above. DeVonta Smith - WR (hamstring) Smith was ruled out for Week 7 on Saturday. Smith has repeatedly aggravated the hamstring strain he initially injured in August. He remains sidelined to begin Week 8 and was ruled out Friday. Impact: Wide receivers Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Britain Covey (knee) are also out for Week 8. Tight end Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon benefit. Tank Bigsby - RB (core) See above. Impact: See above. Jalen Hurts - QB (blood clots) Team doctors discovered a blood clot in Hurts' calf. Impact: See above. ◆ Washington Commanders Terry McLaurin - WR (knee) McLaurin suffered a season-ending patellar tendon rupture in Week 6. Impact: Treylon Burks should step into primary perimeter snaps, although he suffered an apparent injury late in the fourth quarter. No update has been passed on Burks as of Tuesday. Head coach Dan Quinn said he will practice in full on Thursday. Impact: Diggs is a WR4/FLEX if active, while rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams warrants a start in the FLEX spot. Treylon Burks - WR (foot) Burks was limited on Wednesday , did not practice Thursday, and was limited Friday, drawing a questionable tag for Week 8. Impact: Burks does not need to be rostered. NFC North ◆ Chicago Bears Kyle Monangai - RB (thumb/toe) Head coach Ben Johnson labeled Monangai as " day-to-day " with a thumb injury suffered in Week 4, but he was later revealed to have suffered a turf toe injury as well. He remains sidelined for the Bears' Week 7 game against the Patriots on Thursday . He was ruled out for Week 8 Saturday. Impact: D'Andre Swift is an RB1. Roschon Johnson can be stashed. Impact: Expect Sam Roush to serve as the team's TE2 for the remainder of the season, while second-year tight end Colston Loveland should continue his recent ascension back into TE1 territory. ◆ Detroit Lions Isiah Pacheco - RB (back) Pacheco was placed on injured reserve to start the season. There appears to be something more insidious going on with Pacheco's back than initially thought. Lions coach Dan Campbell said running backs Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could split touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs . Saylors appears to be the first player up. Gibbs handled an absurd 34 opportunities, of 37 total running back opportunities, in the team's Week 1, overtime win over the Saints Amon-Ra St. Brown - WR (ankle) St. Brown picked up a minor ankle injury in Week 7. Head coach Dan Campbell said Tuesday that the veteran receiver "should be fine" for Week 8 against the Vikings. He did not practice on Wednesday but finished the week with two full sessions, carrying a clean designation into the weekend. Impact: None. Jahmyr Gibbs - RB (shoulder) Gibbs did not practice on Wednesday but practiced in full Thursday and Friday. He will play in Week 8. Impact: Head coach Dan Quinn told reporters that he wanted to get some of his players "off their feet" Wednesday, so sidelining Gibbs could just be a precautionary move. ◆ Green Bay Packers Matthew Golden - WR (shoulder/foot) Golden gutted through multiple injuries on Thursday Night Football. Impact: None. Impact: Beyond the football implications, it is good to hear Reed avoided any life-altering injuries in Week 2. Skyy Moore and Bo Melton are likely to soak up additional snaps, although volume is most likely to concentrate on Christian Watson , Matthew Golden , and Tucker Kraft . Impact: Brooks had been the most consistent rusher in a timeshare situation. Skyy Moore - WR (ankle) Moore sported a walking boot instead of practicing on Wednesday . He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday . Impact: Should he miss time, the Packers' star players would further consolidate touches. ◆ Minnesota Vikings Aaron Jones - RB (knee) Jones sustained a knee injury in Week 7 and was unable to finish the game. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. Impact: None. ◆ New Orleans Saints Travis Etienne - RB (hamstring) Etienne aggravated his hamstring injury in the team's Week 3 loss to the Raiders. Impact: Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller appear likely to split the load in Etienne's absence, neither of whom is overly enticing in fantasy circles in what is expected to be a shared workload. Jordyn Tyson - WR (hamstring) Tyson begins the regular season on injured reserve . Impact: Tyson is trending toward returning following the Saints' Week 8 bye. ◆ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Jalen McMillan - WR (knee) McMillan suffered a sprained PCL in his first game action of the season in Week 3. The team placed him on injured reserve Monday, with an expected absence of 6-8 weeks. Impact: Not much change considering he made his season debut in Week 3, although rookie Ted Hurst should remain in the starting lineup. Emeka Egbuka - WR (foot/concussion) Egbuka was ruled out for Week 7 on Friday. He was limited to begin Week 8 but was ruled out due to his foot injury Friday. Kenneth Gainwell - RB (hip) Gainwell suffered a hip injury in Week 7 and was sidelined to begin Week 8, ultimately drawing the questionable tag for Week 8. Impact: Bucky Irving should handle a larger-than-normal workload if Gainwell is sidelined. Sean Tucker can be stashed on benches. NFC West ◆ Arizona Cardinals Jeremiyah Love - RB (ankle) Love was sidelined throughout Weeks 6 - 7 . Impact: None. ◆ Los Angeles Rams Terrance Ferguson - TE (ankle) Ferguson aggravated an ankle injury in the team's Week 3 loss to the Broncos and was sent to injured reserve . Impact: The hits to the San Francisco pass catchers continue as Evans now appears to be in line to miss at least Week 7. The team has its bye in Week 8, potentially setting up a situation where Evans misses only one contest. Expect volume to concentrate on Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle, with the team also expected to be without Deebo Samue l for their game against the Falcons. Expect Mike Evans , assuming health, Christian McCaffrey , and George Kittle to soak up additional volume. He will resume practicing in Week 8 and could face the Bears on Monday night. The team removed him from the injury report Saturday although they have yet to activate him from injured reserve. Impact: Price appears set to return to a primary role for the Seahawks, although fantasy managers will want to confirm he is activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday night.

stories.title: Adam Thielen explains issues between Aaron Rodgers and DK Metcalf
stories.summary: Adam Thielen seems to know why Rodgers and Metcalf have struggled to get on the same page.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s safe to say that DK Metcalf’s first season in a Pittsburgh Steelers uniform was far from a success. The receiver posted just 850 yards after being suspended for the team’s final two regular-season games, and struggled to find consistency with quarterback Aaron Rodgers all season. Many believed the additions of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard, coupled with the continued development of Roman Wilson, would alleviate some of the pressure and focus put on Metcalf by opposing defenses. However, it has been a modest at best start to the season for the receiver, as he has posted just 374 yards through the team’s first seven games. Appearing on ESPN’s NFL Live, former Steelers wide receiver Adam Thielen addressed why he believes the connection between Rodgers and Metcalf still has yet to hit its full stride. “What Aaron likes is he likes to have guys just line up and play football,” Thielen said. “We’re not going to move him around. We’re not going to put him in the slot. We’re not going to motion him. We just want to line up and go win.DK is not that guy. He’s not a guy you just put out there at the X, and it’s third and five, and you go win, right? And you’re seeing that on the tape. You’re seeing that it’s he’s looking for him. He wants him, but he’s not open. And that’s okay. Some guys just aren’t that guy. You got to be able to move them around. You got to be able to put them in stacks. You got to be able to motion them. But he’s not that guy right now in this offense.” Thielen appeared in five games for the Steelers last season, recording 11 receptions for 117 yards. Coming from someone who played with the duo last season, this observation holds more weight than your normal sports talking head. The receiver struggled with drops early in the season, but has found some consistency by going over 90 receiving yards in two of his last four games. Something still feels off with the connection between the Steelers quarterback and their top wideout. One former receiver believes it’s due to Metcalf’s lack of versatility overall. Metcalf’s only game of over 100 yards this season happened to come against Cleveland. Metcalf and Rodgers will have to be in sync to help the Steelers win this game and earn sole possession of first place in the AFC North, but it may not be that simple. stories.title: 1 thing I loved, 3 things I hated: Michigan Football at Rutgers
stories.summary: The run game struggled, the pass game flashed, and the kicking game is broken. Here is 1 thing we loved and 3 things we hated from Michigan Football vs Rutgers:
stories.detailText: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 31: Wide receiver Jourdin Houston #4 of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights makes a catch for a touchdown defended by Cornerback Smith Snowden #3 of the Michigan Wolverines during the second quarter at SHI Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Mark Smith/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images The Michigan Wolverines sure do like to keep fans on the edge of their seat, don’t they? After a barnburner against Indiana last week, they kept things interesting once again as they took on Rutgers for a Halloween matinee. The Scarlet Knights were only down by one point at halftime and kept things real close in the second half. However, after Rutgers was able to tie the game in the fourth quarter, Michigan was able to put one more score on the board and win the game by a final score of 28-21. As has been the case in every game this year, this wasn’t the prettiest one to watch. Here is one thing I loved and three things I hated from today’s game. 1 thing I loved: Success in the pass game Even though quarterback Tommy Carr was battling a case of the flu heading into this game, he played really well for the most part. Carr was 13-of-16 for 184 yards and one touchdown at the halftime break, with his longest play going for 44 yards to fellow freshman Salesi Moa. TOMMY CARR TO SALESI MOA FOR 44 YARDS pic.twitter.com/XWIf2tdKMK — Barstool Michigan (@BarstoolUofM) October 31, 2026 Carr’s pass to JJ Buchanan for a touchdown to finish that drive was also a thing of beauty from both the quarterback and the wide receiver. MICHIGAN SCORED A TOUCHDOWN!! JJ BUCHANAN 92 YARDS PRAISE THE LORD https://t.co/dtH6UWnkG1 pic.twitter.com/zv6gjGMBfa — Barstool Michigan (@BarstoolUofM) October 31, 2026 Carr ended the game 21-of-26 for 257 yards and that one touchdown. When the Wolverines needed a big play on offense on Saturday, Carr was the one delivering for his team. 1 thing I hated: Defensive drives extended due to penalties Whittingham has talked quite a bit this season about limiting penalties on both sides of the ball. Unfortunately, the defense was flagged for a pair of 15-yard penalties on the first two drives of the game for Rutgers to keep its offense on the field. First, on the very first play from scrimmage of the game, cornerback Smith Snowden was called for roughing the passer after going low on Rutgers quarterback AJ Surace. It was a bit questionable, but the 15 yards gave Rutgers an automatic first down at its own 40 yard line just a few seconds into the game. Then, on Rutgers’ second offensive drive, cornerback Jyaire Hill was flagged for pass intereference on star wide receiver KJ Duff. Following that play, Rutgers only had 12 total yards at the time, while the Michigan defense had been penalized for 30 yards. The Scarlet Knights were able to get a field goal on this drive, and it very likely would not have happened had it not been for the penalty. Here's another look at the injury to KJ Duff on that last play. 👉 https://t.co/ec6OiV2SfM pic.twitter.com/UjfZxMpLjx — Rutgers Scarlet Knights | The Knight Report (@RutgersOn3) October 31, 2026 Fast forward to the second quarter, and the Wolverines were up 14-10 with about five minutes left. Michigan’s offense was hoping to get the ball back once more with plenty of time left in the half, but unfortunately, Snowden was called for a holding penalty on 3rd-and-4. That drive ended in yet another field goal to cut Michigan’s lead to just one point, 14-13. After Michigan went up 28-21 late in the fourth quarter, Zeke Berry was called for pass interference on the very first play of the ensuing Rutgers drive, giving the Scarlet Knights much better field position in an effort to tie the game. It didn’t result in points being put on the board, but that would have been a back-breaker had Rutgers managed to go down the field and score a touchdown. Jay Hill has done wonders with this defense this season, but this was a really frustrating game for that side of the ball, as they kept the Scarlet Knights’ offense on the field for much longer than it should have been. The defense also gave up more than 20 points for the first time all season. The offense has gotten a lot of flack (reasonably so) this year — and the offense had its own penalty problems right before halftime — but the defensive penalties continue to stack up and are a big problem. Another thing I hated: The run game struggled…again Michigan’s run game has been pretty bad all season long — No. 101 in the FBS heading into this one, to be exact. But going into a game against the No. 129 overall rush defense in the FBS, most fans and pundits alike expected the Wolverines to get things going in the ground game against the Scarlet Knights. Instead, Jordan Marshall, Savion Hiter and Bryson Kuzdzal continued to struggle producing chunk plays on the ground. The longest run of the game went for just 15 yards (Carr’s touchdown run) and the team averaged 3.6 yards per carry. Hiter led the group with 20 carries for 76 yards, while Kuzdzal took six carries 37 yards, and Marshall had five carries for zero yards. Those are embarrassing numbers when you’re going up against one of the worst run defenses in all of college football. I can’t imagine the run game will be much better against any of the four remaining opponents on the schedule this year. A final thing I hated: Trey Butkowski is broken After missing a pair of field goals last week against the Hoosiers, sophomore kicker Trey Butkowski missed two more field goals in this game — one from 48 yards out and other from 35 yards out. He has now missed four of his last six field goal tries. For the first time in a long time, Michigan has a very legitimate problem at kicker. Trey Butkowski yanks a 35-yarder wide left, his fourth miss in the past seven quarters. pic.twitter.com/VNXzl7CCW8 — Tony Garcia | Detroit Free Press (@RealTonyGarcia) October 31, 2026 The really unfortunate part about all this is Butkowski had not missed a single kick up until last week’s game. Now, the Wolverines all of a sudden have a kicking problem. That’s to go along with the punt return issues that have plagued the team this season — the Wolverines ranked No. 102 in the country (6.4 yards per punt return) heading into this game. For as nice as it was to get a legitimate special teams coordinator on the coaching staff in Kerry Coombs late last year, it sure hasn’t resulted in much success in 2026. Hopefully Butkowski turns things around soon because his services will be needed against teams like Ohio State, UCLA and even Michigan State. There are a few other things I hated from this game, but I’m curious to hear what you guys have to say. What did you love and hate from the Rutgers game? Let me know down in the comments below!

stories.title: NFL to review additional allegations against Packers RB Josh Jacobs
stories.summary: The NFL said it will look into additional allegations of physical and verbal abuse by Packers RB Josh Jacobs that were revealed as part of a public records release from the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department.
stories.detailText: The NFL said Saturday it will look into additional allegations of physical and verbal abuse by Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs that were revealed as part of a public records release from the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department. The allegations, released Friday night in response to a public records request, show that three women alleged abuse by Jacobs to the department in incidents dating back to April 2021. The women came forward after learning of Jacobs' arrest in connection with an alleged domestic violence incident in May. "We will review these allegations as part of the investigation which has remained open," the NFL said in a statement. Along with the allegations made by the three women, police released reports from the investigation as well as body camera and police dash camera footage from Jacobs' arrest. He pleaded no contest to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property. "The Brown County District Attorney's office had these uncorroborated, old, and previously unreported allegations for months," Jacobs' attorneys, David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III, said in an emailed statement Saturday. "They conducted their own exhaustive investigation, along with the police department, and the D.A. determined that only two misdemeanor charges were warranted. They then entered into a plea agreement with Josh Jacobs. Josh has repeatedly expressed his remorse and is honoring the terms of the agreement." In the 129-page report of the incident released Friday night -- some of which was heavily redacted -- the woman making the initial accusations against Jacobs told police he "looked like a different person" during the alleged battery and said he attempted to strangle or suffocate her two times. She told police it was the first time he had ever strangled or suffocated her. In the report, police wrote that she "described Joshua's demeanor as 'enraged' and said she thought she was going to die." A 911 call from the May 23 incident released by police Friday evening showed yelling in the background by a male, but no one spoke with police before the line was disconnected. Police were then dispatched to the address about a possible disturbance. The woman alleged the incident began when she accused Jacobs of speaking with other women. When the woman tried to leave the home, the report alleged, Jacobs would initially not let her, broke her phone and eventually grabbed her by the neck in the garage and slammed her to the ground, hitting her head on the concrete floor and causing her to lose consciousness. When she woke up, the report claimed she told police it was hard for her to walk, she had blurry vision and she was "seeing dots/stars" in her vision. The police department withheld some records, including surveillance video from the garage where part of the alleged incident occurred. Both Jacobs and the woman sued the police department to block the release of the records. In a letter explaining the withholding, the department said it "would have released the garage video, with the victim's entire body being pixelated," had it not been restricted from doing so. After the incident, the woman went to a neighbor's home for help, according to the report. Police interviewed two of the woman's friends who communicated with her by phone and text message in the hours following the incident about what occurred, according to the documents. The reports from the friends mirrored what the woman told police, although neither friend was present during the incident and both based their statements on what the woman told them during those phone conversations. After Jacobs was arrested after a car he was a passenger in was pulled over May 26, he told officers that he didn't have identification on him and that he had already given his cellphone to his attorneys because he was planning on turning himself in. As Jacobs arrived at the police station after being transported there by police, he was read his Miranda rights, and he told the arresting officer he did not want to make a statement until his lawyer arrived. Jacobs then proceeded to have a brief conversation with the arresting officer, according to footage released from the police car. Jacobs: "In this situation, right, if I know I'm 100% didn't do anything wrong, what can I do in a situation to, like, you know, avoid it. To me, it's like, unfair, you know what I'm saying. So I don't really understand." Officer: "It's up to your lawyer. He gets paid a s--- ton more than I do. He does his thing." Jacobs: "I'm saying like legally, though, if I was to call, it wouldn't have made a difference and I would still be the one." Officer: "Remember, these charges aren't set in stone. They are referrals." Jacobs: "It's just what they think. OK." Officer: "So there's a chance you could get convicted. There's a chance they could be dropped. These are referred to the [district attorneys] saying this is what we've got based upon our initial investigation. It's up to the DA and the judges to do what they want with it." The officer then closed the door for a few moments before Jacobs was led out of the police car.

stories.title: Colton Joseph gets benched as Badgers get embarrassed in another Iowa game
stories.summary: The Badgers struggles against Iowa continued on Saturday.
stories.detailText: MADISON, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 19: Colton Joseph #1 of the Wisconsin Badgers drops back to pass against the Eastern Michigan Eagles at Camp Randall Stadium on September 19, 2026 in Madison, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a 24-7 win over the No. 16 USC Trojans last weekend, there was optimism that a leaf had turned for the 5-2 Wisconsin Badgers coming into a rivalry game against the Iowa Hawkeyes. Unfortunately, it was more of the same, as the Badgers were embarrassed by Iowa for the third straight year, losing 30-0. Now, in four games against Iowa under Luke Fickell, Wisconsin has been outscored 124-16. The Badgers started the game on defense and were heading towards a three-and-out, but Matt Jung took a poor angle in coverage on a tight end wheel route and was beaten badly, leading to a wide-open receiver for a huge gain on 3rd & 7. Iowa saw some success in the run game, mixing in a reverse to their tight end, but the Badgers were able to get back-to-back stops in the run game in the red zone to force a field goal. Wisconsin’s offense started backwards, as Colton Joseph took a bad sack on 1st & 10 rather than throwing it away or getting the ball out quicker. That essentially killed the drive, as Wisconsin had a short quarterback run on 2nd down and minimal gain on a tight end screen on third, thanks to a high throw from Joseph and a missed block. Iowa started cooking on the drive after, although it was nearly another three-and-out again, as Wisconsin got Iowa into 3rd & 6. But Matt Jung triggered late to a receiver at the sticks, allowing the first down. From there, Iowa really started cruising, with Hank Brown making some nice plays with both his arms and legs, while the run game started getting some big holes. This was just a masterful drive from Iowa offensive coordinator Tim Lester, who schemed a number of open receivers, with Brown finding his tight end up the seam for a touchdown on third and goal. Wisconsin went backwards again on its next drive with a pair of false starts, resulting in a quick three-and-out, but the Badgers defense got a key stop. After a Jai’mier Scott pass interference, the Badgers were able to get Iowa off the field thanks to a sack by Sebastian Cheeks on 3rd & 10 at the 50-yard line. Iowa still caught a break, though, as Xavier Williams coughed up the ball on a hit from Cooper Catalano, but the Hawkeyes recovered. They ended up punting. The Badgers really started to move the ball for the first time all game, going 12 plays and 86 yards after starting at their own 12-yard line. Wisconsin had an 18-yard completion to Chris Brooks on 3rd & 13, and a huge 41-yard catch from Jaylon Domingeaux got the Badgers into a goal-to-go situation. But Wisconsin could not punch it in on four straight runs, including a poor 4th-and-1 play call at the 1-yard line that resulted in a loss of two. To make matters worse, Iowa took the stop and went seven plays for 98 yards and a touchdown, dicing up Wisconsin’s defense in the air again to increase their lead to 17-0 with under 90 seconds left in the half. The Badgers had no urgency to score on their next drive, going for back-to-back runs, and Colton Joseph fumbled on second down without being touched, giving Iowa an easy opportunity for a field goal to end the half. Down 20-0, the Badgers started the second half with the ball and moved the ball initially with a 15-yard completion to Jaylon Domingeaux. But Wisconsin stalled there, going for a one-yard run before two incompletions to punt it back. Then, it was the same story again. The Badgers got Iowa into a 3rd & 7, only this time it was a penalty that extended the drive for Iowa with Jai’mier Scott being flagged for holding. It was poor defense the rest of the drive, as Iowa’s run game moved the Badgers, and they continued to repeat similar concepts all the way to their third touchdown. Just like that, it was 27-0, and the Hawkeyes were in full control midway through the third. It was another rough series for Colton Joseph, as he had an incompletion to Jaylon Domingeaux before failing to step up in a clean pocket on third down, instead bailing and getting zero yards for another punt. Iowa started at their own 40-yard line and got two first downs thanks to their run game before settling for a field goal to make it 30-0. Joseph had yet another three-and-out and it wasn’t pretty. He wasn’t close on a 1st-down throw, which wouldn’t have mattered thanks to an ineligible man downfield penalty. Then, on 3rd down, he was way high on a back shoulder to Jaylon Domingeaux. If there was one player who fought his heart out on Saturday, it was Sebastian Cheeks, who forced an incompletion on what would’ve likely been a huge gain with a big hit on first down. Wisconsin forced a three-and-out and elected to bench Colton Joseph for Ryan Hopkins for the final quarter plus. Hopkins got three drives and ended up going 8 for 13 for 93 yards and an interception, compared to Joseph’s 92 yards on 5 of 14 passing. Iowa held out for the 30-0 win, extending the win streak to five games, and there are now serious questions for the Badgers, starting at the quarterback position and extending to the coaching staff. Next up for the Badgers is a home game against Rutgers, as Wisconsin has to look itself in the mirror once again.
